lessons.OUT_OF_MONEY: Visitors must show they can support themselves for the whole stay. Most people underestimate rent, transit and winter clothes in their first months.
lessons.STAY_EXPIRED: Visitors are usually allowed up to six months. You can apply to extend before your status expires; staying past it without applying makes you out of status.
lessons.BURNOUT: Job hunting without the right to work is exhausting. Settlement agencies, libraries and newcomer job programs are free, and most are open to visitors.
lessons.UNAUTHORIZED_WORK: Working as a visitor, even cash shifts or an 'unpaid trial', is unauthorized work. It can lead to removal and make future applications fail.

lessons.BURNOUT: Newcomers in their first five years have had far higher unemployment than people born in Canada. Settlement agencies, food banks, EI and free counselling exist for the hard months; using them is not failure.

options.feedback: One more call log, one less headache.

options.label: Argue with Aunty for two hours
options.feedback: Aunty wins. Aunty always wins.

items.title: Anniversary video call
items.body: Your spouse plans a surprise call with both families. Screenshots for the file, joy for you.

LAGOS_YABA_DAWN.title: Generator coughs. Light dies.
LAGOS_YABA_DAWN.speaker: {area}, {city}
LAGOS_YABA_DAWN.dialogue: NEPA has packed up. Your neighbour is already in a Europe group chat. Downstairs, {area} is waking. {RelWho} in {relCity} sent three missed calls. Everybody don japa. This year na your turn, or another send-forth you go attend.

choices.text: {Bus} to {jobPlace} and hunt {jobHunt}
Call {relTitle} in {relCity} about the visa story
Sleep. Waka the street when dusk is cheaper.

LAGOS_JOB_BOARD.title: Four hundred applicants. One reply.
LAGOS_JOB_BOARD.speaker: {techHub}
LAGOS_JOB_BOARD.dialogue: Application forty. {jobListing}, and {relName} typing 'have you left the house??' from {relCity}.

choices.text: Rewrite the CV the Canadian way: two pages, no photo, no date of birth
{Bus} to the 'visa consultant' whose status is all approval screenshots
Go back to {area} and rethink the whole plan

LAGOS_AUNTY_CALL.title: {RelName} does not sugarcoat.
LAGOS_AUNTY_CALL.speaker: {relCity} × {area} FaceTime
LAGOS_AUNTY_CALL.dialogue: {RelPoss} window in {relCity} shows {relWeather}; {relSubj} is {relGap}. Yours is generator light. {RelSubj} will write an invitation letter for a visitor visa: a visit, not a job. {RelSubj} will not lie on a bank statement. 'Bring your own proof, {name}, or don't come and disgrace me at Pearson.'

choices.text: Leave the call. Go to the annex and start a real paper trail
Ask {relObj} to lend you the showing-money
Sell your Corolla on Jiji to fund your own proof of funds
choices.label: SELL_CAR

LAGOS_YABA_DUSK.title: The street is louder than your plan.
LAGOS_YABA_DUSK.speaker: {market}, at the edge
LAGOS_YABA_DUSK.dialogue: Pepper soup steam, {bus} horns, a preacher on a megaphone. People are going somewhere: work, church, the park, abroad in their heads. {RelName}'s last voice note is still unplayed.

choices.text: Catch another {bus} to the job hunt
Step aside and call {relName} properly
Keke to a weekend gig in {gigArea}

success.feedback: Cash in hand, two new clients from the market WhatsApp group.
success.label: PAID_IN_FULL

fail.feedback: The client said 'I will send it Monday.' It is now three Mondays later.
fail.label: I_WILL_SEND_IT_MONDAY

choices.text: Answer the Facebook ad: 'Canada Caregiver Visa in 4 Weeks. Office in {city}'
choices.label: AGENT_ROOM_AD

LAGOS_CV_NIGHT.title: The document starts to look like a person.
LAGOS_CV_NIGHT.speaker: {area} room, 3 a.m.
LAGOS_CV_NIGHT.dialogue: You put numbers on every year of your work. You hide the generator. A recruiter in Toronto replies. {RelName} is on a night shift in {relCity}; {relPoss} status still says 'call me when light comes.'

choices.text: Take the interview. Buy data. Set two alarms.

success.feedback: They loved {interviewHook}. A second call with the hiring manager is booked for tomorrow.
success.label: GOT_THE_OFFER

fail.feedback: NEPA took the light mid-answer. They went with someone in Mississauga. You learn how to fail politely.
fail.label: NEPA_STRIKES

choices.text: Ghost it and go back to the street

LAGOS_AGENT_OFFICE.title: The office smells like toner and panic.
LAGOS_AGENT_OFFICE.speaker: Agent's office, {city}
LAGOS_AGENT_OFFICE.dialogue: He talks fast: Schengen, Canada express, 'we know people at the High Commission'. There is no licence on the wall. {RelName} would shout if {relSubj} saw this receipt.

choices.text: Pay his 'facilitation' fee so your file 'moves faster'
choices.label: PAID_FACILITATION

choices.text: Walk out and pay a CICC-licensed consultant's ₦150k deposit instead (check the public register first)
choices.label: LICENSED_RCIC
choices.feedback: Expensive, but the licence number is real and checkable. Paid representatives must be licensed by the CICC (or be lawyers).

choices.text: Walk out and do it yourself: IRCC's own checklist and {relName} on video
choices.label: DIY
choices.feedback: Free, slower, and every mistake is yours. Plenty of people do it this way.

LAGOS_DOCUMENT_GRIND.title: Photocopies, stamps, another queue.
LAGOS_DOCUMENT_GRIND.speaker: Immigration annex, Alausa
LAGOS_DOCUMENT_GRIND.dialogue: Bodies in a line that does not move and also never ends. A clerk calls names like a {bus} conductor. {RelName} texts a photo of the invitation letter, snow on the window behind {relObj}.

choices.text: Book the appointment: CAD 185 in visa and biometrics fees. {Bus} to the visa centre
Envelope too thin. Keke to the weekend hustle
Pay the tout at the gate who promises your new passport 'tomorrow' for ₦250k
choices.label: PASSPORT_TOUT

choices.text: Follow the man who says he has a passport with a Canada visa already inside. 'The face resemble you well well'

LAGOS_SHOWING_MONEY.title: Love, with conditions.
LAGOS_SHOWING_MONEY.speaker: WhatsApp: {relName} & the family group
LAGOS_SHOWING_MONEY.dialogue: {RelName} will send a statement snapshot, not a transfer. 'If they ask whose money, tell the truth.' Uncle in Abuja laughs from the group chat: Canada is for people with uncles in Canada.

choices.text: Accept {relName}'s documented host support and build an honest file around it
choices.feedback: A host's letter and their own statement, labelled as theirs, are legitimate support for a visitor visa. Borrowed money shown as yours is not.

choices.text: Borrow a friend's statement and go anyway
choices.label: MISREPRESENTATION
choices.feedback: Submitting someone else's bank statement as your own is misrepresentation.

LAGOS_WEEKEND_GIG.title: Cash in the pocket. Dust in the lungs.
LAGOS_WEEKEND_GIG.location: Rain in {gigArea}, then a keke home
LAGOS_WEEKEND_GIG.speaker: Rain in {gigArea}, then the okada home
LAGOS_WEEKEND_GIG.dialogue: {gigWork}, then two Bolt trips in the rain. The envelope thickens. A woman under a shop awning is shouting into her phone the same way you shout to {relName}: 'I am coming. Traffic.'

choices.text: Bank it. {Bus} to the paperwork
Go home and spend some on a sharper CV and LinkedIn
One more weekend. Waka back to {area}.

LAGOS_BERLIN_CALL.title: 3:05 p.m. The call connects.
LAGOS_BERLIN_CALL.speaker: {area}, on borrowed light
LAGOS_BERLIN_CALL.dialogue: Toronto asks about {interviewStory}. Then: '{offerCatch}' {RelName} is on speaker from a {relCity} bus: 'Say yes. I go dey wait for you when you land.'

choices.text: Take the offer. Apply for the work permit once their LMIA comes through
choices.feedback: A job offer needs a work permit, not a visitor visa. Working on a visitor visa is unauthorized work.

choices.text: Start your nursing college registration, and visit {relName} on a visitor visa while it runs
choices.label: REGISTER_FIRST
choices.feedback: The honest order for nurses: registration first, then a job offer and work permit. The visit is just a visit.

choices.text: Panic. Go back to the street and call {relName} later
Ask if they'll hire you through the Global Talent Stream: for tech roles the LMIA can take about two weeks
choices.label: GLOBAL_TALENT
choices.feedback: They're a Global Talent Stream employer: the LMIA targets about 10 business days for in-demand tech jobs, at the going wage, with a plan to train Canadians. Then your work permit application.

LAGOS_EMBASSY_QUEUE.title: Token number 47.
LAGOS_EMBASSY_QUEUE.speaker: Visa Application Centre, {vacCity}
LAGOS_EMBASSY_QUEUE.dialogue: Plastic chairs. Token numbers. Fingers on glass, one photo, done in ten minutes. Nobody here decides anything: the real decision happens in an office you'll never see, on what you uploaded.

choices.text: Check every upload with {relName} on video first: names, dates, stamps, all matching
choices.label: CLEAN_FILE
choices.feedback: Officers want relevant and organized. Yours reads like one person's life.

choices.text: Upload everything you own, just in case: 90 pages
choices.label: KITCHEN_SINK
choices.feedback: Officers want relevant and organized, not a 90-page PDF.

LAGOS_DECISION_GATE.title: They take your fingerprints. You keep your passport.
LAGOS_DECISION_GATE.speaker: Outside the centre, VI sun
LAGOS_DECISION_GATE.dialogue: You step into the heat. {RelName} is already ringing. Your file is a visitor visa on {relPoss} invitation, or a work permit if the job came through. Canada only asks for your passport after a yes: a 'passport request', so the visa can be stuck inside it. Express Entry people call theirs the famous PPR; yours works the same way. You go home and live inside a status page.

choices.text: Pick {relName}'s call, then wait with the phone on loud

LAGOS_OUTCOME.title: A text at 11:41 p.m.
LAGOS_OUTCOME.speaker: {area} mattress, phone glowing
LAGOS_OUTCOME.dialogue: {RelName} is typing. The IRCC portal says 'New message'. A passport request for your visa sticker, or a refusal letter? If not, you are still here, which is not the same as finished.

choices.text: Open the portal. Call {relName} either way.

LAGOS_ENDING_WIN.title: Visa in hand.
LAGOS_ENDING_WIN.speaker: Airside, {airportCode} → the glass
LAGOS_ENDING_WIN.dialogue: Plastic tray. Stamped page. {RelName} is on FaceTime from Pearson arrivals in a future you have not reached yet, and also from {relCity} right now, crying and laughing. You go. That is the deal.

outcome.title: Visa in hand
outcome.lesson: A visitor visa lets you travel to Canada to visit, not to work or stay, and the officer at Pearson still decides. Since 28 August 2024 visitors can't apply for a work permit from inside Canada: a job means a work permit, applied for properly.

LAGOS_ENDING_STAY.title: The country keeps you.
LAGOS_ENDING_STAY.speaker: {area}, same generator, new month
LAGOS_ENDING_STAY.dialogue: {RelName} does not drop the call. 'We try again. I am not going anywhere.' Rice that tastes like delay. Tomorrow you can try another corridor. People do.

outcome.title: The country keeps you
outcome.lesson: Most applications that fail can be made again. A refusal letter usually names the reason (funds, ties, purpose); fix that reason before you pay another fee.

SUV_PITCH_START.speaker: Ms. Vance (Committee Chair)
SUV_PITCH_START.dialogue: Thank you for the presentation. Your fintech concept for sub-Saharan trade looks interesting on paper. However, Canada's regulatory market is heavily protected, and compliance here is notoriously brutal. Why should we back an unproven foreign platform over an established local player?

choices.text: Nigeria's fintech sector is much faster and more innovative than Canada's. Our tech is simply superior.
choices.label: ARROGANCE TRAP
choices.feedback: That dismissed the panel's knowledge of their own market.

choices.text: We don't compete with banks. Canadian exporters settle West African invoices in minutes, not 48 hours.
choices.label: HIGH VALUE MATCH
choices.feedback: You framed it as direct economic value for Canada.

choices.text: We already have 40 Nigerian customers; Canada is just a new market for us
choices.label: WRONG_MARKET
choices.feedback: Real traction, but they want to hear what you'll build in Canada.

SUV_PITCH_START.title: The pitch.

SUV_PITCH_CHEN.speaker: Dr. Chen (Chief Technology Officer)
SUV_PITCH_CHEN.dialogue: Let's look at your architecture. Your platform handles high-volume cross-border ledger balances. If the data pipes fail or a severe bottleneck occurs between {city} and Toronto, how does your ledger protect financial integrity without crashing performance?

choices.text: We use advanced cloud systems and high-end security encryption to make sure everything stays secure and never crashes.
choices.label: TECHNICAL DROPOUT
choices.feedback: You did not answer the architecture question.

choices.text: Queued, event-driven settlement. If the link drops, transactions wait, then settle and reconcile.
choices.label: CRITICAL CRUISE
choices.feedback: A precise answer. It also took real effort to deliver.

choices.text: Honestly, we've never had a serious outage. Our uptime speaks for itself
choices.label: UNTESTED
choices.feedback: True, and it's not an answer. Dr. Chen writes something down.

SUV_PITCH_CHEN.title: The architecture question.

SUV_PITCH_ROSS.speaker: Mr. Ross (Managing Partner)
SUV_PITCH_ROSS.dialogue: Your team listing shows four co-founders, all in {city}. If we issue a Letter of Support, the core team must relocate to Canada to scale this business. What happens if your Lead Developer decides to stay behind or fails their immigration check?

choices.text: That won't happen. We are best friends from university and fully committed to moving together. We trust each other completely.
choices.label: BUSINESS RISK
choices.feedback: Investors back contingency plans, not friendships.

choices.text: Key-person clause, documented code, and a vetted backup developer already in Canada.
choices.label: OPERATIONAL FAILSAFE
choices.feedback: That showed institutional maturity.
choices.lockedHint: Your CTO left this week. There's no backup to claim

choices.text: Be straight: our CTO left this week. Kemi built the settlement queue, and here's her plan and our hiring budget
choices.label: HONEST_GAP
choices.feedback: Mr. Ross respects it. 'Every startup loses someone. Most hide it.'

choices.text: Our lead dev will stay in Lagos and work remotely; that's cheaper
choices.label: REMOTE_DEV
choices.feedback: Cheaper, but the program wants the business run from Canada.

SUV_PITCH_ROSS.title: The team question.

SUV_LOS_ISSUED.speaker: Maple Venture Incubator
SUV_LOS_ISSUED.dialogue: The committee votes yes. A Letter of Support is on its way. This is the first step of a long process: the Letter of Support is required, but it does not by itself grant permanent residence.

outcome.title: LETTER OF SUPPORT ISSUED
outcome.subtitle: The committee backs your startup. Now the real paperwork begins.
outcome.lesson: A Letter of Support is only step one: IRCC still assesses the business, the founders' funds and admissibility. Heads-up: the Start-up Visa stopped taking new commitment certificates on 1 January 2026, and founders with a 2025 certificate had until 30 June 2026 to apply. A replacement entrepreneur program has been announced but not launched. Check canada.ca.

SUV_LOS_ISSUED.title: Letter of Support.

SUV_PITCH_FAIL.speaker: Maple Venture Incubator
SUV_PITCH_FAIL.dialogue: The committee passes on your pitch. You lose ₦500,000 in incorporation and consulting fees, and the Startup Visa route is blocked for now.

outcome.title: Committee passes
outcome.lesson: Designated organizations choose businesses they believe in; nobody can legitimately sell you a Letter of Support. Ads promising one for a fee are a common scam. Heads-up: IRCC has paused new Start-up Visa applications; this route shows how the pitch worked. Check canada.ca for the current entrepreneur programs.
outcome.subtitle: The pitch wasn't ready. The scam ads will say otherwise.

SUV_PITCH_FAIL.title: Committee passes.

LMIA_INTERVIEW_KOVACS.speaker: Mr. Kovacs (Operations Director)
LMIA_INTERVIEW_KOVACS.dialogue: You've run bigger fleets than ours. That's rare. But you're on a visitor record and I need someone Monday. This is a supervisor role above the provincial median wage, so it's the high-wage stream. Why should I pay a lawyer and wait months for you?

choices.text: Tell him your cousin's company got an LMIA in three weeks, so it's easy
choices.label: CRITICAL LEAK
choices.feedback: Overconfident, and he's done this before. Employers know the LMIA is slow and expensive.

choices.text: Give me two weeks on your backlog and you'll see the LMIA fee pay for itself
choices.label: HIGH ROI MATCH
choices.feedback: You framed the legal cost as an operating saving.

LMIA_INTERVIEW_KOVACS.title: Mr. Kovacs.

LMIA_ADVERTISING.speaker: Mr. Kovacs (Operations Director)
LMIA_ADVERTISING.dialogue: The numbers make sense. But Service Canada requires me to show I advertised this job to Canadians and permanent residents, for at least four weeks, and couldn't find a qualified person. Wey Sabi says everybody just posts a fake ad. How do we do this?

choices.text: We can post a fake job listing with impossible requirements so no Canadian qualifies and the government has to approve my file.
choices.label: LEGAL HAZARD
choices.feedback: Suggesting fraud to a legitimate employer ends the conversation.

choices.text: Your freight runs through West African corridors. If the role genuinely needs knowledge of those trade compliance frameworks, that requirement can be documented in the posting.
choices.label: RISKY GAMBLE
choices.feedback: A requirement written to fit one candidate gets scrutinised. Service Canada asks why a Canadian couldn't learn it.

choices.text: Let's follow the advertising rules exactly. I'll help you document the real requirements of the role and any recruitment you've already done.
choices.label: COMPLIANT PATH
choices.feedback: Slower, but nothing here can be used against either of you.

LMIA_ADVERTISING.title: The advertising question.

LMIA_FRAUD_FAIL.speaker: Mr. Kovacs
LMIA_FRAUD_FAIL.dialogue: Mr. Kovacs stands up. 'This interview is over.' Had that posting been filed, it would have been misrepresentation, with a possible five-year ban.

outcome.title: Blatant Misrepresentation
outcome.lesson: Lying in an interview that feeds an immigration application is misrepresentation too. Employers verify, and IRCC can refuse and bar you for five years.

LMIA_FRAUD_FAIL.title: Interview over.

LMIA_SPONSORSHIP.speaker: Mr. Kovacs
LMIA_SPONSORSHIP.dialogue: Kovacs nods slowly. 'Send me what you have. I'll talk to our immigration lawyer.' A sponsorship offer is not a work permit yet, but you are in the process.

outcome.title: EMPLOYER WILL SPONSOR
outcome.subtitle: The LMIA process starts. The clock is still running.
outcome.lesson: An employer willing to apply is the start. The LMIA itself is the employer's application to ESDC, the employer pays its fee, and charging a worker for it is illegal.

LMIA_SPONSORSHIP.title: He'll sponsor.

LMIA_DECLINED.speaker: Mr. Kovacs
LMIA_DECLINED.dialogue: 'I like you, but it's too much risk for us right now.' The interview ends politely and the clock keeps ticking.

outcome.title: No Sponsorship
outcome.lesson: Most employers never sponsor: the LMIA costs them time, a CAD 1,000 fee and proof that no Canadian could do the job. Low-wage LMIAs are also paused in high-unemployment cities since 2024.

LMIA_DECLINED.title: Too much risk.

TOURIST_HUB.speaker: The 180-Day Tourist Gamble
TOURIST_HUB.dialogue: You landed on a visitor record with savings, a cousin's couch and a plan: find an employer willing to start an LMIA before your time runs out. Visitors can network and interview. Visitors cannot work. Mentor Wey Sabi keeps saying one word: Kawosoke.

actions.label: Attend In-Person Tech/Job Fair
consequences: You collected 14 tote bags, 3 stress balls and one real business card. It belongs to a recruiter from your own village.
A booth handed you a free hoodie. It is the warmest thing you own.
You queued 40 minutes for the Shopify booth. They were out of stickers and jobs.
leadConsequences: A logistics director asked for your CV, then your WhatsApp. Then actually replied. Lead acquired.

actions.label: Cold Message 10 Hiring Managers
consequences: 9 left you on 'seen'. One replied: 'Wrong person, I sell insurance. Are you covered?'
LinkedIn suggested you 'Open to Work' harder. You are already wearing the green banner like a cape.
A recruiter replied with a thumbs-up emoji and nothing else. You have analysed it for three hours.
leadConsequences: An operations manager in Mississauga wrote back: 'Can you talk Thursday?' You screamed into a cushion.

actions.label: Coffee Chat with a Naija-Canadian Mentor Wey Sabi
actions.blurb: Tim Hortons, double-double on you. Wey Sabi knows everything (Wey Sabi says)
consequences: Wey Sabi has been here 11 years. First advice: 'Buy proper boots.' Second: 'Stop saying sir.' Third, in a whisper: 'Kawosoke. Everybody dey do am.'
Wey Sabi spent 40 minutes on Canadian work culture, 20 on why Jollof here is a scandal, and 5 on a 'paralegal' who sells asylum stories. You did not ask.
Wey Sabi says: 'This LinkedIn thing is slow. Raise your hands, Kawosoke, collect work permit.' Wey Sabi has never read the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act.
leadConsequences: Wey Sabi forwarded your CV to an old manager. 'He owes me a favour.' For once, Wey Sabi actually sabi.

actions.label: Answer the WhatsApp: 'Positive LMIA, CAD 25k Only'
actions.blurb: A cousin's friend's agent. 'Calgary warehouse, approved LMIA, pay in naira'
consequences: The voice note is very confident. The LMIA number is 'coming'.

actions.label: Reply to 'Caregiver Sponsorship, ₦600k Training Fee'
actions.blurb: A Facebook ad says Canadian families need nannies NOW
consequences: The page has 40,000 followers and a lot of stock photos of smiling grandmothers.

actions.label: Coffee with Kunle from Ibadan
actions.blurb: He says he 'has news' about his job
consequences: He slides his phone across the table.

actions.label: Canadianize Your Resume
actions.blurb: Delete the passport photo, add metrics
consequences: You removed your photo, date of birth and state of origin. It already looks 40% more Canadian.
Your 4-page CV is now 2 pages. You mourn the loss of 'Hobbies: Reading and Travelling'.

actions.label: Rest on Cousin's Couch
consequences: Your cousin's wife asked, very politely, about 'your timeline'.
You slept 11 hours. The kids have started calling you 'Uncle Couch'.

actions.label: Talk to Your Cousin About the Couch
actions.blurb: Month three. His wife has stopped greeting you
consequences: The parlour feels smaller every week.

actions.label: Kawosoke: Claim Asylum Inside Canada
actions.blurb: Wey Sabi's favourite advice. The IRCC portal, from the couch
consequences: You open the IRCC portal. The form wants every address you have had since you were 18.

actions.label: Take a Cash Warehouse Shift (Under the Table)
actions.blurb: CAD 14 an hour, cash, 'no SIN, no wahala'
consequences: The agency man counts the van seats twice.

actions.label: Book the Flight Home, Record Clean
actions.blurb: No LMIA, no lies, no overstay
consequences: Your cousin drives you to Pearson in silence.

TOURIST_HUB.title: 180 days, one couch.

TOURIST_WIN.speaker: Northline Logistics
TOURIST_WIN.dialogue: Mr. Kovacs at Northline Logistics wants to meet you.

outcome.title: You got the meeting
outcome.subtitle: The Hidden LMIA Interview is unlocked. Your desperation walks in with you.
outcome.lesson: Visitors may look for work and attend interviews, but may not start working. If an employer gets an LMIA, the work permit is normally applied for from outside Canada, so the honest win often means flying home to wait.

TOURIST_WIN.title: The meeting.

LAGOS_MISREPRESENTATION.title: The statement wasn't yours.
LAGOS_MISREPRESENTATION.speaker: Visa Application Centre, {vacCity}
LAGOS_MISREPRESENTATION.dialogue: Weeks later, a letter. The officer compared the account name with your passport and asked where the money came from. A borrowed bank statement is misrepresentation, and that can bar you from applying for five years.

outcome.title: Flagged for misrepresentation
outcome.lesson: Borrowed or 'parked' money shown as your own is misrepresentation under section 40 of IRPA: refusal plus a five-year ban on applying. Officers ask for the source of large recent deposits.

EE_START.title: The calculator says {crs}.
EE_START.speaker: {area}, {city}
EE_START.dialogue: You are {age}, with {educationPhrase} and {experiencePhrase}. The IRCC calculator is blunt: without a language test or an Educational Credential Assessment (ECA), your Comprehensive Ranking System score is {crs}. Every point from here has to be earned.

choices.text: Book IELTS General Training and study for three months first
choices.label: PREPARED

success.feedback: L8.5 R8 W7 S7.5: CLB 9 or better in every ability. Three months of evenings paid off.
success.label: CLB_9

fail.feedback: L8 R7 W6.5 S7. Writing missed CLB 9 by half a band: CLB 8 for now.
fail.label: ONE_BAND_SHORT

choices.text: Book the test for Saturday. How hard can it be?
choices.label: RUSHED

success.feedback: You're one of those people who are good at exams. CLB 8 with zero preparation.
success.label: EXAM_PERSON

fail.feedback: The writing task was about 'a community garden'. CLB 6: below the CLB 7 Federal Skilled Worker minimum. You can't enter the pool on that yet.
fail.label: CLB_6

choices.text: Book PTE Core instead: computer-based, results in days
choices.label: PTE_CORE
choices.feedback: PTE Core has counted for Express Entry since 2024. Half the group chat writes it now.

success.feedback: PTE Core: CLB 9. Results in two days, screenshot in the group chat in two minutes.

fail.feedback: CLB 7. Enough for the pool, not enough to be competitive.

choices.text: Pay an agent who 'guarantees' Band 8 with a leaked paper
choices.label: FRAUD

choices.text: Book CELPIP-General in Lagos or Ibadan: computer-based, Canadian accents, and the score is the CLB level
choices.label: CELPIP
choices.feedback: Myth check: CELPIP doesn't earn fewer points than IELTS. Express Entry converts every test to a CLB level, and CELPIP 9 is CLB 9, the same as IELTS L8, R7, W7, S7.

success.feedback: CELPIP: 9 in every skill. CLB 9, the same CRS points as the IELTS bands everyone fights for.
success.label: CLB_9

fail.feedback: CELPIP: 8 in listening, 8 in writing. CLB 8 for now.
fail.label: CLB_8

choices.text: Book a Wednesday date and sneak out of work for the morning
choices.label: WEEKDAY_TEST

success.feedback: Oga is in Abuja. You're back by 1 p.m. with a story about the bank. CLB 8.
success.label: SNUCK_OUT

fail.feedback: Server crash at 8:15. Oga: 'Nobody leaves this office.' You miss the test, lose the fee, and rebook for a Saturday. You write it tired: CLB 7.
fail.label: EMERGENCY

EE_ECA.title: Transcripts, sealed and direct.
EE_ECA.speaker: School registry, {city}
EE_ECA.dialogue: WES will only accept transcripts sent directly by your school. The registry window says six to eight weeks. Without the ECA, your education is worth zero points.

choices.text: Pay the official express transcript fee and courier
choices.label: PAID_THE_PROPER_FEE
choices.feedback: WES confirms the Canadian equivalent of your education, and it unlocks transferability points.

choices.text: Go back every week and follow up in person
choices.label: PERSISTENCE

success.feedback: On the fifth visit, the registrar finds your file under a calendar. Sealed, stamped, sent to WES.
success.label: PERSISTENCE_PAID

fail.feedback: ASUU strike. Registry closed. Come back next month.
fail.label: ASUU_STRIKE

choices.text: Ask a 'connect' to print a transcript tonight
choices.label: FRAUD

EE_PROFILE.title: You are in the pool.
EE_PROFILE.speaker: IRCC portal
EE_PROFILE.dialogue: Profile submitted. Your CRS is on the meter above, with the breakdown under it. Draws in 2026 have mostly been category-based: Canadian Experience Class around 507-523, French-language draws between 382 and 420, and provincial nominee draws far higher because a nomination adds 600 points.

choices.text: Refresh the rounds page on draw night

EE_PROFILE_UPDATE.title: Profile updated.
EE_PROFILE_UPDATE.speaker: IRCC portal
EE_PROFILE_UPDATE.dialogue: The new score is in. The next round of invitations is days away.

choices.text: Refresh the rounds page on draw night

EE_BELOW.title: Not this round.
EE_BELOW.speaker: IRCC portal
EE_BELOW.dialogue: This round: Canadian Experience Class, cutoff 518. French draws went down to the 380s for NCLC 7. Healthcare sat around 470 and trades around 476, if you have 6 months of continuous experience in a listed job in the last 3 years. What now?

choices.text: Enrol at the French institute: nine months to NCLC 7 (TEF Canada)
choices.label: FRENCH_PIVOT

success.feedback: TEF Canada: NCLC 7 in all four abilities. French draws are open to you now.
success.label: NCLC_7

fail.feedback: NCLC 5. Some points, but the French-language draws need NCLC 7 in every ability.
fail.label: NCLC_5

choices.text: Retake IELTS and push for CLB 10
choices.label: RETAKE

success.feedback: CLB 10. Every ability, every point.
success.label: CLB_10

fail.feedback: Same score, new receipt. Language points don't move without new preparation.
fail.label: SAME_SCORE

choices.text: Work a second year in Canada, then update your profile
choices.label: CANADIAN_EXPERIENCE
choices.feedback: Canadian experience is worth more each year, and it maxes out your transferability points.
choices.lockedHint: Needs at least one year of Canadian work experience

choices.text: Apply to your province's Express Entry stream
choices.label: PROVINCIAL_NOMINATION
choices.lockedHint: Provinces are mostly choosing people already working there

success.feedback: Nominated. +600 points. In 2026 most provinces favour people already working there.
success.label: NOMINATED

fail.feedback: Not selected this intake. Provincial streams fill fast, and most now favour people already working there.
fail.label: NOT_THIS_INTAKE

choices.text: Do a master's in Canada instead (Student route)
choices.label: SWITCH_ROUTES

choices.text: Rest for a month and reset
Pay an agent for a 'job offer' to add points
choices.label: FRAUD

EE_FRENCH.title: Bonjour, NCLC 7.
EE_FRENCH.speaker: French institute, {city}
EE_FRENCH.dialogue: Nine months of evenings, verb tables on the {bus} and one very patient Madame Leclerc. You are also nine months older: after 29, every birthday costs CRS points. Check the meter.

choices.text: Update your profile with the TEF Canada results
Use your French for a Francophone Mobility work permit: a job outside Quebec, no LMIA needed
choices.label: FRANCO_MOBILITY

EE_ITA_FRENCH.title: Invitation to apply!
EE_ITA_FRENCH.speaker: IRCC portal
EE_ITA_FRENCH.dialogue: French-language proficiency draw. Your score clears the cutoff. You have 60 days to submit a complete application for permanent residence.

choices.text: Start the application

EE_ITA_CEC.title: Invitation to apply!
EE_ITA_CEC.speaker: Toronto
EE_ITA_CEC.dialogue: Canadian Experience Class draw. Your Canadian work experience carried you over the cutoff. 60 days to submit.

choices.text: Start the application

EE_ITA_PNP.title: Invitation to apply!
EE_ITA_PNP.speaker: IRCC portal
EE_ITA_PNP.dialogue: Provincial nominee draw. With 600 nomination points, the cutoff was never in doubt. 60 days to submit.

choices.text: Start the application

EE_FUNDS.title: Proof of funds.
EE_FUNDS.speaker: Bank, {city}
EE_FUNDS.dialogue: Federal Skilled Worker applicants must show settlement funds in their own name: CAD $15,263 for one person (the figure in use since July 2025). Borrowed money does not count. Canadian Experience Class applicants are exempt.

choices.text: Submit six months of statements
choices.label: FUNDS_PROVEN
choices.feedback: Steady savings with a clear history.
choices.lockedHint: Needs CAD $15,263 in savings

choices.text: You're applying under the Canadian Experience Class: no funds needed
choices.label: CEC_EXEMPT
choices.feedback: CEC applicants do not need to show settlement funds.
choices.lockedHint: Only for Canadian Experience Class

choices.text: Family gift: parents transfer savings with a signed gift letter and their bank records
choices.label: DOCUMENTED_GIFT
choices.feedback: Gifted funds count when they are documented and truly yours to keep. +CAD 6,000.
choices.lockedHint: The family has given what it can

choices.text: Work overtime for four more months and save
choices.label: SAVING_UP
choices.feedback: Four months of overtime: +CAD 3,000. The balance climbs; so does the tiredness.

choices.text: Take a week off before the 60-day deadline
choices.label: BREATHER
choices.lockedHint: Only when you're running low
choices.feedback: You slept. The documents are still there. So are you.

choices.text: Borrow from your cousin for a week to show the balance
choices.label: FRAUD

EE_DOCS.title: Police certificate. Medical. Uploads.
EE_DOCS.speaker: Police command, {city}
EE_DOCS.dialogue: A police character certificate through the Nigeria Police online portal (when it is up), a medical with an IRCC panel physician when IRCC asks for it, and every document uploaded within 60 days of the invitation.

choices.text: Queue for the certificate and book the panel physician properly
choices.label: DONE_RIGHT

choices.text: The police portal is down for weeks: submit on time with proof you applied and a letter of explanation
choices.label: LOE_SUBMITTED
choices.feedback: IRCC accepts proof that a police certificate was requested when it can't arrive in time. Missing the deadline is worse.

choices.text: Pay someone to 'skip' the medical
choices.label: FRAUD

EE_COPR.title: Welcome to Canada.
EE_COPR.speaker: Toronto Pearson
EE_COPR.dialogue: PPR at last: IRCC's passport request. Your passport goes to the visa centre in {vacCity} and comes back with a permanent resident visa inside, plus your Confirmation of Permanent Residence (COPR). At the airport the officer checks both, stamps the papers and says the words: welcome to Canada. You are a permanent resident.

outcome.title: Permanent resident
outcome.lesson: Permanent residence comes after the ITA, a complete application (police certificates, medical, funds, reference letters) and months of processing. Keep living in Canada at least two of every five years to keep it.

EE_SWITCH.title: Plan B is a classroom.
EE_SWITCH.speaker: Toronto
EE_SWITCH.dialogue: You switch to the Student route. A Canadian credential adds points, and the post-graduation work permit gives you the Canadian experience that Express Entry rewards most.

outcome.title: Switching to the Student route
outcome.lesson: Canadian education plus a year of Canadian work is the most common way people now get invited: Canadian Experience Class draws have dominated since 2024.

EE_CANADA_START.title: PGWP in hand.
EE_CANADA_START.speaker: Toronto
EE_CANADA_START.dialogue: You graduated, got your post-graduation work permit and found a full-time job {canadaJob}. Express Entry counts Canadian work in full years.

choices.text: Work a full year, then create your Express Entry profile
choices.label: CANADIAN_EXPERIENCE
choices.feedback: One year of skilled Canadian work: +40 points and more transferability.

EE_FRAUD_IELTS.title: The paper was never leaked.
EE_FRAUD_IELTS.speaker: IELTS Test Centre
EE_FRAUD_IELTS.dialogue: The 'leaked paper' was last year's practice test. Your result is flagged for review, and test fraud is reported. Misrepresentation can bar you from Canada for five years.

outcome.title: Flagged
outcome.lesson: Test providers and IRCC check results directly. A 'leaked paper' is almost always a scam, and test fraud can lead to a misrepresentation finding.

EE_FRAUD_DOCS.title: The document was fake.
EE_FRAUD_DOCS.speaker: {city}
EE_FRAUD_DOCS.dialogue: IRCC verifies documents with the issuing body. A forged document is misrepresentation: refusal and a five-year ban.

outcome.title: Flagged for misrepresentation
outcome.lesson: IRCC can verify transcripts, reference letters and certificates with the issuer. A forged document is misrepresentation: refusal and a five-year ban.

EE_FRAUD_JOB.title: There is no job.
EE_FRAUD_JOB.speaker: IRCC portal
EE_FRAUD_JOB.dialogue: The 'employer' does not exist. Since March 25, 2025 a job offer adds no CRS points anyway, and a fake one is misrepresentation.

outcome.title: Flagged for misrepresentation
outcome.lesson: Since March 25, 2025 a job offer adds no CRS points. Anyone still selling a 'job offer for points' is selling nothing, and a fake offer is misrepresentation.

EE_FRAUD_FUNDS.title: Whose money is this?
EE_FRAUD_FUNDS.speaker: Bank, {city}
EE_FRAUD_FUNDS.dialogue: The officer asks for the source of a large recent deposit. Borrowed funds presented as savings is misrepresentation.

outcome.title: Flagged for misrepresentation
outcome.lesson: Express Entry proof of funds must be your own and available, usually shown with about six months of statements. Borrowed money does not count.

EE_BURNOUT.title: You ran out of you.
EE_BURNOUT.speaker: {area}, {city}
EE_BURNOUT.dialogue: You stop opening the portal for a month. Your profile is still in the pool, but you have nothing left for it. Rest first.

outcome.title: Burnout
outcome.lesson: An Express Entry profile stays in the pool for 12 months. Waiting is normal; burning out is optional. Rest, then update the profile.

ST_START.title: Three admission emails.
ST_START.speaker: Cyber cafe, {area}
ST_START.dialogue: The most common route to Canada starts with a classroom. Your inbox has offers. Choose carefully: the program decides your tuition, your funds and whether you get a post-graduation work permit (PGWP).

choices.text: {mastersProgram}, public university (16 months, CAD 32,000 for year one)
choices.label: MASTERS
choices.feedback: Since January 1, 2026, master's and PhD students at public institutions don't need a provincial attestation letter, and the master's PGWP isn't tied to a field-of-study list.
choices.lockedHint: Needs a completed bachelor's degree (or equivalent)

choices.text: Four-year bachelor's in Computer Science, public university (CAD 35,000 a year)
choices.label: BACHELORS
choices.feedback: A Canadian bachelor's counts as 3+ years of Canadian education: the most CRS points for study in Canada.

choices.text: {diplomaProgram}, public college (CAD 18,000 a year)
choices.label: COLLEGE
choices.feedback: College diplomas must be on IRCC's field-of-study list for a PGWP. Check the program's CIP code.

choices.text: One-year certificate at a cheap private career college (CAD 9,000)
choices.label: CHEAP_OPTION
choices.feedback: Cheaper. Read the PGWP rules before you pay.

choices.text: An agent promises a 'guaranteed admission letter' from a top university for N2.5M, no transcripts needed
choices.label: FRAUD

choices.text: Chase a fully funded research master's: email professors directly
choices.label: SCHOLARSHIP_ROUTE
choices.lockedHint: You need a first degree for a research master's

ST_LOA.title: Letter of acceptance.
ST_LOA.speaker: {area}, {city}
ST_LOA.dialogue: Your letter of acceptance arrives from a designated learning institution. If your program needs a provincial attestation letter (PAL), the school requests it from the province. In 2026 most master's and doctoral students at public institutions are exempt.

choices.text: Work out the money

ST_FUNDS.title: Show the money.
ST_FUNDS.speaker: Bank, {city}
ST_FUNDS.dialogue: You need first-year tuition, CAD 23,448 for living costs (applications from September 1, 2026) and money for travel. Officers also check where the money came from, so big recent deposits need a paper trail. Bachelor's: about CAD 60,500. Master's: about CAD 57,500. College: about CAD 43,500. Private certificate: about CAD 34,500.

choices.text: Apply for the entrance scholarship (write the essay tonight)
choices.label: SCHOLARSHIP
choices.lockedHint: You already applied

success.feedback: Entrance scholarship: CAD 7,500 off tuition. Officers like a school that bets on you.
success.label: SCHOLARSHIP_WON

fail.feedback: A polite 'we received many strong applications'. The essay is still yours to reuse.
fail.label: NOT_THIS_YEAR

choices.text: Family sponsorship: Daddy and {uncle} sign letters with their statements and source of funds
choices.label: FAMILY_SPONSOR
choices.lockedHint: The family has given what it can

choices.text: Sell the plot in the village (deed and sale agreement as proof of source)
choices.label: SOLD_THE_LAND
choices.feedback: CAD 12,000, documented. Your mother cried, then helped with the paperwork.
choices.lockedHint: The land is already sold

choices.text: Crowdfund on X and WhatsApp
choices.label: CROWDFUNDED
choices.lockedHint: You already ran the campaign

choices.text: Education loan from a lender that funds international students (approved for your school)
choices.label: EDUCATION_LOAN
choices.feedback: A loan from a financial institution is accepted proof of funds. Repayments start after graduation.
choices.lockedHint: You already have the loan

choices.text: Ask a friend to 'park' N25M in your account for two weeks
choices.label: FRAUD

choices.text: The funds are ready: book biometrics and submit (CAD 57,448 for the master's)
choices.lockedHint: Needs CAD 57,448: first-year tuition plus CAD 23,448 to live on

choices.text: The funds are ready: book biometrics and submit (CAD 60,448 for the bachelor's)
choices.lockedHint: Needs CAD 60,448: first-year tuition plus CAD 23,448 to live on

choices.text: The funds are ready: book biometrics and submit (CAD 43,448 for the college diploma)
choices.lockedHint: Needs CAD 43,448: first-year tuition plus CAD 23,448 to live on

choices.text: The funds are ready: book biometrics and submit (CAD 34,448 for the private certificate)
choices.lockedHint: Needs CAD 34,448: first-year tuition plus CAD 23,448 to live on

choices.text: Defer a year: work, save, and apply next intake
choices.label: DEFERRED
choices.feedback: A year of savings with a real history behind it. Officers like that more than a sudden deposit.

ST_FUNDS_SHORT.title: The numbers don't add up yet.
ST_FUNDS_SHORT.speaker: Bank, {city}
ST_FUNDS_SHORT.dialogue: Tuition plus CAD 23,448 plus travel is more than you can show. An application without enough funds is refused, and the refusal stays on your record.

choices.text: Back to the funding plan

ST_SOP.title: The study plan.
ST_SOP.speaker: {area}, {city}
ST_SOP.dialogue: The officer will read one document to understand you: your study plan. Why this program, why Canada, and what happens after.

choices.text: Write a specific plan: how the program builds on {sopBackground}, and your career path
choices.label: SPECIFIC_PLAN
choices.feedback: Concrete, consistent with your history, easy to believe. It cost you a week of 2 a.m. nights and a missed shift.

choices.text: Pay an editor in the group chat to polish your draft (CAD 120)
choices.label: EDITOR
choices.feedback: Polished and clean. It also stopped sounding like you.

choices.text: Download a template and change the names
choices.label: TEMPLATE
choices.feedback: Officers read thousands of these. Templates read like templates.

choices.text: Say plainly that the plan is permanent residence
choices.label: DUAL_INTENT
choices.feedback: Wanting PR later is allowed (dual intent), but the officer must still believe the study plan itself.

ST_VFS.title: Biometrics at the VAC.
ST_VFS.speaker: Visa Application Centre, {vacCity}
ST_VFS.dialogue: Fingerprints, a photo, and your passport back in your bag. Canada asks for it only after a yes. The decision depends mostly on your study plan and funds; the odds on the button show where you stand.

choices.text: Wait for the decision

success.feedback: The portal says 'Passport request'. That means yes: the visa sticker goes in your passport, then the letter of introduction follows.
success.label: APPROVED

fail.feedback: Refused. Even a strong file can be refused; a weak one usually is.
fail.label: REFUSED

ST_APPROVED.title: Study permit approved.
ST_APPROVED.speaker: {airport}
ST_APPROVED.dialogue: First the passport request: your passport goes to the visa centre in {vacCity} for the visa sticker. Then the port of entry letter of introduction lands in your inbox. Print it: the CBSA officer at the airport prints your actual study permit from it. {RelName} screams on the phone from {relCity}. Pack for winter.

choices.text: Start packing

ST_REFUSED.title: Refused.
ST_REFUSED.speaker: Your inbox
ST_REFUSED.dialogue: 'I am not satisfied that you will leave Canada at the end of your stay, based on the purpose of your visit.' Two lines. Your family group chat has already seen your face.

choices.text: Ask {relName} in Canada to order your GCMS notes (about 30 days), then fix the reason the officer actually wrote down
choices.label: GCMS_NOTES
choices.feedback: The notes took 30 days, so you missed the January intake. They showed the real concern: the study plan didn't connect to your background. Now you can fix it.

choices.text: Pay a licensed consultant to read the refusal and rework the file (CAD 600)
choices.label: RCIC_REVIEW
choices.feedback: Faster than waiting for notes, and the licence number checks out. Expensive help is still help.

choices.text: Reapply next week with the same file
choices.label: SAME_FILE

choices.text: Pay an agent ₦3 million for a 'guaranteed visa'
choices.label: FRAUD

ST_ARRIVAL.title: Terminal 3, January.
ST_ARRIVAL.speaker: Toronto Pearson
ST_ARRIVAL.dialogue: The officer checks your letter and issues the study permit. Outside it is -18°C and your {city} 'jacket' is a hoodie.

choices.text: New parka and boots from the mall (CAD 350; rent is tight)
choices.label: BOUGHT_PARKA
choices.feedback: Warm, and slightly poorer.

choices.text: Value Village thrift run: CAD 60 for a parka with a suspicious zip
choices.label: THRIFTED

success.feedback: The zip holds. Someone's old Canada Goose, CAD 60. You tell everyone.
success.label: THRIFT_WIN

fail.feedback: The zip dies at the bus stop in week two. You hold it shut with one hand all winter.
fail.label: ZIP_DIED

choices.text: The hoodie will do
choices.label: HOODIE

success.feedback: A mild January day, −4°C. You get away with it. Today.

fail.feedback: −24°C with the wind at the streetcar stop. You can't feel your toes.

ST_TERM.title: First term.
ST_TERM.speaker: Campus, Toronto
ST_TERM.dialogue: Rent is CAD 950 for a basement room, and year-two tuition comes out of your account whatever you choose. Students can work up to 24 hours a week off campus during classes and full-time in scheduled breaks.

choices.text: Campus cafe job, 12 hours a week
choices.label: BALANCED
choices.feedback: Less money, more sleep, better grades.

choices.text: Warehouse nights, the full 24 hours a week allowed off campus
choices.label: MAXED_THE_HOURS
choices.feedback: Legal, tiring, and your grades feel it.

choices.text: Cash shifts, 40 hours a week, no paperwork
choices.label: BREACHED_CONDITIONS

ST_FINALS.title: Finals week.
ST_FINALS.speaker: Campus library, Toronto
ST_FINALS.dialogue: Snow outside, coffee inside. Your grades decide whether you graduate on time.

choices.text: Library every night until the last exam
choices.label: LOCKED_IN

choices.text: Pick up extra shifts instead
choices.label: SPLIT_FOCUS

success.feedback: You studied on the bus and somehow it held: grades steady, CAD 1,200 richer.
success.label: HELD_IT_TOGETHER

fail.feedback: You fell asleep in the exam hall. One course failed.
fail.label: SLEPT_IN_THE_EXAM

ST_PGWP_MASTERS.title: Convocation.
ST_PGWP_MASTERS.speaker: Toronto
ST_PGWP_MASTERS.dialogue: Master's degree in hand and a post-graduation work permit approved. A Canadian credential and Canadian work experience are what Express Entry rewards most.

outcome.title: Graduate with a PGWP
outcome.lesson: Master's graduates can get up to a three-year post-graduation work permit, and master's programs are exempt from the field-of-study list.

ST_PGWP_COLLEGE.title: Convocation.
ST_PGWP_COLLEGE.speaker: Toronto
ST_PGWP_COLLEGE.dialogue: Diploma in hand, and because the program is on the field-of-study list, your PGWP is approved. Next: Canadian work experience and Express Entry.

outcome.title: Graduate with a PGWP
outcome.lesson: College graduates now need a program on the field-of-study list (applications since November 2024) and CLB 5 in English or French to get a PGWP.

ST_NO_PGWP.title: No PGWP.
ST_NO_PGWP.speaker: Toronto
ST_NO_PGWP.dialogue: You graduated, but private career college programs are generally not eligible for a post-graduation work permit. Your study permit expires in 90 days.

outcome.title: Graduated, no work permit
outcome.lesson: Programs at private career colleges are generally not PGWP-eligible. Check the school's PGWP status on the DLI list before paying a deposit.

ST_PROBATION.title: Academic probation.
ST_PROBATION.speaker: Campus, Toronto
ST_PROBATION.dialogue: Your grades dropped below the line. You must repeat the term, and the extra tuition is on you.

outcome.title: Academic probation
outcome.lesson: Study permits require you to stay enrolled and make progress. Failing courses costs tuition and can affect your status and later applications.

ST_STATUS_BREACH.title: Out of status.
ST_STATUS_BREACH.speaker: Etobicoke
ST_STATUS_BREACH.dialogue: Working beyond your study permit conditions can cost you your status and future applications.

outcome.title: Study permit conditions breached
outcome.lesson: Off-campus work is capped at 24 hours a week during classes. Working past it breaches your study permit conditions and can end your stay.

ST_FAKE_LOA.title: The letter was fake.
ST_FAKE_LOA.speaker: Agent's office, {city}
ST_FAKE_LOA.dialogue: IRCC now verifies every letter of acceptance directly with the school. A fake one is misrepresentation: refusal and a five-year ban.

outcome.title: Flagged for misrepresentation
outcome.lesson: Since December 2023 IRCC checks every letter of acceptance with the school. In 2023, hundreds of students faced removal over fake admission letters sold by an agent.

ST_FUNDS_PARKING.title: Parked money.
ST_FUNDS_PARKING.speaker: Bank, {city}
ST_FUNDS_PARKING.dialogue: A large deposit two weeks before applying, with no source. Officers ask where it came from, and parked funds presented as your own is misrepresentation.

outcome.title: Flagged for misrepresentation
outcome.lesson: Officers look for a history of savings, not a sudden deposit. Explain every large deposit with a source (salary, sale agreement, loan letter).

ST_BURNOUT.title: Running on empty.
ST_BURNOUT.speaker: Toronto
ST_BURNOUT.dialogue: Exhaustion caught up with you. Rest, then try again.

outcome.title: Burnout
outcome.lesson: Food banks, campus counselling and student associations exist for this. Most international students report that the first winter is the hardest.

ST_PGWP_BACHELORS.title: Convocation.
ST_PGWP_BACHELORS.speaker: Toronto

outcome.title: Graduate with a PGWP
outcome.lesson: Three or more years of Canadian study can mean a three-year PGWP and extra CRS points for Canadian education.

ST_PGWP_BACHELORS.dialogue: Four winters later: a Canadian bachelor's degree and a post-graduation work permit. Three or more years of Canadian study is worth the most CRS points for education in Canada.

TOURIST_ARRIVAL.title: Primary inspection.
TOURIST_ARRIVAL.speaker: Toronto Pearson, Terminal 3
TOURIST_ARRIVAL.dialogue: Nineteen hours and one connection from {airportCode}. The CBSA officer flips through your passport: 'Purpose of your visit?' Wey Sabi's last voice note is still playing in your head: 'As you land, Kawosoke at the airport. No dull yourself.'

choices.text: Tell the truth: a visit, return ticket in hand, savings to show
choices.label: ADMITTED

success.feedback: 'Enjoy your visit.' Six months on your visitor record.
success.label: ADMITTED

fail.feedback: Admitted after two hours in secondary, but the officer writes a three-month limit on your visitor record.
fail.label: THREE_MONTHS_ONLY

choices.feedback: A visitor can stay up to six months, look for work and attend interviews, but cannot work.

choices.text: Kawosoke at the counter: tell the officer you want to claim refugee protection
choices.label: KAWOSOKE_AT_PEARSON
choices.feedback: You can claim at a port of entry. Now the officer has questions, and so will the board.

choices.text: Say you are here for a tech conference you never registered for
choices.label: FRAUD

TOURIST_REFUSED_ENTRY.title: There is no conference.
TOURIST_REFUSED_ENTRY.speaker: Toronto Pearson, secondary inspection
TOURIST_REFUSED_ENTRY.dialogue: The officer searches the conference name. Then your phone. Then your suitcase, which contains eleven printed CVs. Lying to a border officer is misrepresentation: refused entry, and a five-year bar on coming back.

outcome.title: Refused at the border
outcome.subtitle: Misrepresentation carries a five-year inadmissibility. The next flight to {airportCode} has a seat for you.
outcome.lesson: A border officer can refuse entry even with a valid visa. Lying about the purpose of a visit is misrepresentation, with a five-year ban.

KW_POE.title: Secondary inspection.
KW_POE.speaker: Toronto Pearson, CBSA
KW_POE.dialogue: The officer walks you to a side room. Fingerprints, a photo, a long interview. Then the question: 'What do you fear if you return to Nigeria?' Your own story: {kwStory} Wey Sabi's voice note: 'Just pick one.'

choices.text: The truth: nothing will happen to me. I came to find work.
choices.label: HONEST_EXIT
choices.feedback: Refugee protection is for people facing persecution or serious harm at home. Saying so costs you nothing.

choices.text: Buy a ready-made story from Wey Sabi's 'paralegal' (CAD 1,500): LGBTQ, abusive husband or village people, pick from the menu
choices.label: BOUGHT_A_STORY
choices.lockedHint: He wants CAD 1,500 upfront

choices.text: It really happened: you were outed in {area}, beaten, and your photo is in a vigilante WhatsApp group
choices.label: SOGIESC_CLAIM
choices.feedback: Same-sex relationships are criminalized across Nigeria, with penalties of up to 14 years. The board has a guideline for these claims.
choices.lockedHint: That isn't your story. A claim has to be your own

choices.text: It really happened: years of violence from your ex-partner, two police reports that went nowhere, threats from their family
choices.label: GENDER_BASED_CLAIM
choices.feedback: Gender-based violence can ground a claim. The fight will be about state protection and whether you could live safely elsewhere.
choices.lockedHint: That isn't your story. A claim has to be your own

choices.text: It really happened: gunmen attacked your community and you know their names, and they know yours
choices.label: CONFLICT_CLAIM
choices.feedback: Insurgency and banditry are real. The board will ask whether the risk is personal to you, not just general violence.
choices.lockedHint: That isn't your story. A claim has to be your own

choices.text: Tell them what you truly believe: your uncle's juju is after you, and the pastor confirmed it
choices.label: VILLAGE_PEOPLE_CLAIM
choices.feedback: You believe it. The question is whether refugee law covers it.

KW_INLAND.title: The IRCC portal.
KW_INLAND.speaker: IRCC portal, cousin's couch
KW_INLAND.dialogue: The portal wants every address since 18, every trip, every job. A claim made more than a year after you first entered goes to a paper risk assessment, not the board. Then one box: 'What do you fear if you return to Nigeria?' Your own story: {kwStory} Wey Sabi's voice note: 'Just pick one.'

choices.text: The truth: nothing will happen to me. I came to find work.
choices.label: HONEST_EXIT
choices.feedback: Saying so costs you nothing. Note the new rule under Bill C-12: a claim made more than a year after you first entered Canada goes to a paper risk assessment, not the refugee board.

choices.text: Buy a ready-made story from Wey Sabi's 'paralegal' (CAD 1,500): LGBTQ, abusive husband or village people, pick from the menu
choices.label: BOUGHT_A_STORY
choices.lockedHint: He wants CAD 1,500 upfront

choices.text: It really happened: you were outed in {area}, beaten, and your photo is in a vigilante WhatsApp group
choices.label: SOGIESC_CLAIM
choices.feedback: Same-sex relationships are criminalized across Nigeria, with penalties of up to 14 years. The board has a guideline for these claims.
choices.lockedHint: That isn't your story. A claim has to be your own

choices.text: It really happened: years of violence from your ex-partner, two police reports that went nowhere, threats from their family
choices.label: GENDER_BASED_CLAIM
choices.feedback: Gender-based violence can ground a claim. The fight will be about state protection and whether you could live safely elsewhere.
choices.lockedHint: That isn't your story. A claim has to be your own

choices.text: It really happened: gunmen attacked your community and you know their names, and they know yours
choices.label: CONFLICT_CLAIM
choices.feedback: Insurgency and banditry are real. The board will ask whether the risk is personal to you, not just general violence.
choices.lockedHint: That isn't your story. A claim has to be your own

choices.text: Tell them what you truly believe: your uncle's juju is after you, and the pastor confirmed it
choices.label: VILLAGE_PEOPLE_CLAIM
choices.feedback: You believe it. The question is whether refugee law covers it.

KW_NO_CLAIM.title: No claim.
KW_NO_CLAIM.speaker: Brampton
KW_NO_CLAIM.dialogue: You close the portal. Wey Sabi calls you 'too honest for this country'. Your cousin, quietly, is relieved. The clock is still running and the job fair is still on Thursday.

choices.text: Back to the job hunt

KW_FAKE_STORY.title: The 'paralegal' has a menu.
KW_FAKE_STORY.speaker: A back office, Mississauga
KW_FAKE_STORY.dialogue: He is not a lawyer or a licensed consultant, so nobody regulates what he sells. The story fits on one page. The same page, he admits, has been sold forty times this year; he only changes the names. 'Memorize am. No add, no remove.'

choices.text: File it anyway
choices.label: FILED_A_BOUGHT_STORY

choices.text: Walk out. The CAD 1,500 is gone, but so is the trap
choices.label: WALKED_AWAY

choices.text: Report him to the College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants
choices.label: REPORTED
choices.feedback: Only lawyers, Quebec notaries and licensed consultants may charge for immigration advice. He is none of those.

KW_FILED.title: Claim received.
KW_FILED.speaker: Downtown Toronto
KW_FILED.dialogue: Eligibility checked. You get a refugee protection claimant document, Interim Federal Health coverage and an immigration medical booking. Then the question nobody prepared you for: where will you sleep tonight? In 2023 claimants slept on the pavement outside Toronto's shelter intake office until churches opened their halls. The hearing is far away: the board's average wait was well over a year in 2025–2026.

choices.text: Find a lawyer through Legal Aid or a refugee clinic
choices.label: REAL_COUNSEL
choices.feedback: A real lawyer reads your form line by line and starts asking for documents.

choices.text: Pay Wey Sabi's 'paralegal' to 'handle everything'
choices.label: PARALEGAL
choices.feedback: He files nothing. You find out three months later.

choices.text: A Nigerian church opens its hall: a cot, jollof on Sundays, and a pastor who knows a legal clinic
choices.label: SHELTER
choices.feedback: Black churches in Toronto housed hundreds of claimants in 2023, until donations ran out.

KW_WAIT.title: Month 3 of the wait.
KW_WAIT.speaker: Downtown Toronto
KW_WAIT.dialogue: The work permit is still 'in processing'. So is the winter. Your Basis of Claim form is in a file somewhere at the board, and the hearing date is a rumour. How do you spend the wait?

choices.text: Wait for the open work permit (it comes in month 5), then warehouse nights and a PSW course
choices.label: WORKING_LEGALLY
choices.feedback: Legal now. The first paycheque with your own name on it.

choices.text: Take cash warehouse shifts now, before the work permit arrives
choices.label: CASH_JOB

choices.text: Gather evidence: hospital records, police reports, affidavits from witnesses, news from your area
choices.label: EVIDENCE
choices.feedback: Documents from home take months and DHL fees. Each one is a fact the board doesn't have to take on your word.

choices.text: Post your whole claim story on TikTok for sympathy
choices.label: WENT_VIRAL
choices.feedback: Twelve thousand likes. The board can read TikTok too, and the video does not match your form.

choices.text: Ask for your passport back and fly home for {parent}'s 60th. The {partyCloth} is already sewn
choices.label: WENT_HOME

KW_PREP.title: Hearing prep.
KW_PREP.speaker: Refugee clinic, Toronto
KW_PREP.dialogue: The hearing notice came: four weeks. Your counsel puts your Basis of Claim form on the table. 'Read it again. Is every date right?'

choices.text: Go through it line by line and fix the mistakes before the hearing
choices.label: AMENDED
choices.feedback: Correcting the form before the hearing looks honest. Reliving every date costs you a week of sleep.

choices.text: Memorize it word for word, like a WAEC answer
choices.label: MEMORIZED
choices.feedback: Board members can tell a memory from a script.

choices.text: Skip prep. You know your own life
choices.label: WINGED_IT

KW_HEARING.title: Room 7.
KW_HEARING.speaker: Immigration and Refugee Board, Toronto
KW_HEARING.dialogue: A board member, your counsel, a recorder. The member asks about the night it happened, then asks the same question a different way twenty minutes later. Wey Sabi's advice, in your head: 'Cry small. Add pepper.'

choices.text: Answer what you remember, and say 'I don't remember' when you don't
choices.label: STRAIGHT_ANSWERS
choices.feedback: Gaps you admit are human. Gaps you fill with new details are not.

choices.text: Add a new detail to make it stronger
choices.label: EMBELLISHED
choices.feedback: 'Why is this not in your Basis of Claim form?' There is no good answer to that question.

choices.text: Cry on cue, the way Wey Sabi coached
choices.label: PERFORMED

KW_IFA.title: 'Why not Port Harcourt?'
KW_IFA.speaker: Immigration and Refugee Board, Toronto
KW_IFA.dialogue: The member believes what happened to you. Then the question that decides many Nigerian claims: internal flight alternative. 'Could you live safely somewhere else in Nigeria? Lagos? Abuja? Port Harcourt?'

choices.text: Explain, with your evidence, why they would find you anywhere, or why the law follows you everywhere
choices.label: ANSWERED_IFA

success.feedback: Your evidence shows who is looking for you and how far they reach. The member nods slowly.
success.label: IFA_ANSWERED

fail.feedback: The member writes something down and doesn't look up. 'Port Harcourt is a large city.'
fail.label: NOT_CONVINCED

choices.text: Say Lagos is too expensive and the traffic is wicked
choices.label: TRAFFIC_DEFENCE
choices.feedback: Expensive and annoying is not the same as unsafe or unreasonable.

KW_ACCEPTED.title: Protected person.
KW_ACCEPTED.speaker: Immigration and Refugee Board, Toronto
KW_ACCEPTED.dialogue: The member gives the decision at the end of the hearing: you are a Convention refugee. Your counsel squeezes your hand. Next: apply for permanent residence as a protected person. One warning: do not renew your Nigerian passport and do not fly home for Christmas. Going back can cost you the protection. {RelName} is already crying on the phone from {relCity}.

outcome.title: Protected person
outcome.subtitle: Your real story, told straight, with evidence. Permanent residence is next.
outcome.lesson: Refugee protection rests on a real fear of persecution or serious harm, told consistently and backed by evidence. Protected persons can apply for permanent residence, but returning to the home country or renewing its passport can cost them the protection.

KW_FAKE_EXPOSED.title: Three versions of one night.
KW_FAKE_EXPOSED.speaker: Immigration and Refugee Board, Toronto
KW_FAKE_EXPOSED.dialogue: The member asks the name of the street where it happened. You give the paralegal's version, then your own, then a third. The member has seen this page before, with other names on it. Refused, and found manifestly unfounded: no appeal to the Refugee Appeal Division, and a removal order. Every invented LGBTQ or abuse story makes it harder for real ones to be believed.

outcome.title: Bought story, refused
outcome.subtitle: Manifestly unfounded. No appeal, removal, and the paralegal has already sold your page to someone else.
outcome.lesson: Board members hear the same template stories many times. A fabricated claim can be found manifestly unfounded (no appeal to the Refugee Appeal Division), and fake claims make it harder for real ones to be believed.

KW_VILLAGE_REFUSED.title: The board does not cover village people.
KW_VILLAGE_REFUSED.speaker: Immigration and Refugee Board, Toronto
KW_VILLAGE_REFUSED.dialogue: The member is very polite. Refugee protection covers persecution for race, religion, nationality, political opinion or membership in a particular social group, or a personal risk to life the state can't protect you from. 'Your uncle's spiritual attacks are none of those.' Refused.

outcome.title: Refused: no nexus
outcome.subtitle: Village People Interference: 100%. Appeal options exist, but the juju is not a Convention ground.
outcome.lesson: Refugee protection covers persecution for race, religion, nationality, political opinion or membership in a particular social group, or a personal risk the state can't protect you from. Spiritual attacks rarely meet that test.

KW_REFUSED.title: Refused.
KW_REFUSED.speaker: Immigration and Refugee Board, Toronto
KW_REFUSED.dialogue: The decision comes by mail: the member did not find your account credible. You can appeal to the Refugee Appeal Division, then ask the Federal Court to review it. If those fail, a pre-removal risk assessment, then a removal date. Years, spent on a story that did not hold together.

outcome.title: Refused on credibility
outcome.subtitle: Inconsistencies, embellishments and a TikTok. The appeal clock starts now.
outcome.lesson: Most refused claims fail on credibility: dates, places and details that change between the form, the interview and the hearing. Correct mistakes before the hearing, not during it.

KW_REFUSED_IFA.title: Believed, but refused.
KW_REFUSED_IFA.speaker: Immigration and Refugee Board, Toronto
KW_REFUSED_IFA.dialogue: The member believes you were harmed. But without enough evidence that they could find you anywhere, the member finds you could live safely in another Nigerian city. Internal flight alternative. You can appeal, and your counsel thinks there are grounds.

outcome.title: Internal flight alternative
outcome.subtitle: Believed, refused. More evidence of who is looking for you might have changed it.
outcome.lesson: For many Nigerian claims the deciding question is internal flight alternative: could you live safely in another city? Evidence of who is looking for you, and how far they can reach, decides it.

KW_ABANDONED.title: The owambe was lovely.
KW_ABANDONED.speaker: {airport}
KW_ABANDONED.dialogue: You flew back to the country you told Canada you feared. The photos of you dancing at the owambe end your story.

outcome.title: Claim over
outcome.subtitle: Going home to the place you fear tells everyone you don't fear it.
outcome.lesson: Claimants usually hand their passport to the authorities. Travelling back to the country you fear is strong evidence that you don't fear it, and it can end your claim.

EE_ITA_HEALTH.title: Invitation to apply!
EE_ITA_HEALTH.speaker: IRCC portal
EE_ITA_HEALTH.dialogue: Healthcare and social services draw. The cutoff landed around 470, far below the general rounds, because Canada needs nurses. 60 days to submit. In the group chat, someone types 'ITA don land!!!' with nine crying emojis.

choices.text: Start the application

EE_ITA_TRADES.title: Invitation to apply!
EE_ITA_TRADES.speaker: IRCC portal
EE_ITA_TRADES.dialogue: Trades draw. Electricians, welders, plumbers: the cutoff sat around 476 this year. Your certificate finally outranks a master's degree. 60 days to submit.

choices.text: Start the application

ST_PGWP_LANG.title: One more test.
ST_PGWP_LANG.speaker: Test centre, Toronto
ST_PGWP_LANG.dialogue: Since November 2024 a post-graduation work permit needs a language test: CLB 7 for a university degree, CLB 5 for a college program. Your classmate says 'we studied in English, they will understand'. They will not.

choices.text: Book IELTS General Training and prepare for three weeks
choices.label: BOOKED_THE_TEST
choices.feedback: CLB 9. It counts again later for Express Entry.

choices.text: Skip it. Studying in English is proof enough
choices.label: SKIPPED_TEST

ST_NO_PGWP_LANG.title: Missing language test.
ST_NO_PGWP_LANG.speaker: IRCC portal
ST_NO_PGWP_LANG.dialogue: The PGWP application asks for a test result you do not have. Refused. Your study permit expires in weeks, and booking a test now means results after it does.

outcome.title: PGWP refused
outcome.subtitle: No language test, no PGWP. A three-week study plan would have saved two years.
outcome.lesson: Since November 1, 2024 a PGWP needs a language test: CLB 7 for university graduates, CLB 5 for college graduates. Book it before your final term ends.

FY_LANDING.title: Landing day.
FY_LANDING.speaker: Toronto Pearson, Terminal 3
FY_LANDING.dialogue: Welcome to Canada, as a new permanent resident. You have savings, two suitcases and a list of things everyone forgot to tell you: SIN, bank, phone, health card, a place to live, a coat. {RelName} is calling from {relCity}. What do you do first?

choices.text: Get your SIN at the airport Service Canada desk, then open a newcomer bank account this week
choices.label: ADMIN_FIRST
choices.feedback: Your Social Insurance Number lets you work and get paid. Order matters: SIN, bank, phone, then a lease.

choices.text: Buy the best phone plan in the mall so you can call home properly
choices.label: BIG_PLAN
choices.feedback: Video calls home, CAD 95 a month, a two-year contract. Your landlord will still ask for credit history.

choices.text: Winter coat and boots first; everything else can wait a day
choices.label: COAT_FIRST
choices.feedback: Warm feet change everything. A coat drive or thrift store would have halved the bill.

FY_HOUSING.title: Six months upfront.
FY_HOUSING.speaker: Brampton
FY_HOUSING.dialogue: You have no Canadian credit history. The first landlord wants six months' rent in advance. The second listing is a shared basement bed for CAD 375. A Facebook 'landlord' who is 'out of the country' wants a deposit before a viewing.

choices.text: Offer a bank letter, a job-search plan and a guarantor from the {faithHub}
choices.label: GUARANTOR
choices.feedback: First and last month, a reference from someone with Canadian credit. In Ontario, a landlord can't demand more than first-and-last as a deposit.

choices.text: Take the CAD 375 basement bed: three people, one bathroom, no lease
choices.label: BUNK_BED

success.feedback: Crowded but stable. Nobody inspects anything.
success.label: STABLE_ENOUGH

fail.feedback: City inspection: illegal unit, everyone out in 48 hours. Another deposit, another move.
fail.label: INSPECTED

choices.text: Send the Facebook 'landlord' a CAD 1,500 deposit so nobody else gets it
choices.label: RENTAL_SCAM
choices.feedback: There was no landlord. Never pay before a viewing, and check that the person owns the property.

FY_JOBS.title: No Canadian experience.
FY_JOBS.speaker: Brampton Public Library
FY_JOBS.dialogue: Application number forty. The rejection says what the last thirty-nine meant: 'We are looking for candidates with Canadian experience.' Back home you were {occupation}. Here, you are a file with no references.

choices.text: Take a warehouse survival job, nights, and keep applying by day
choices.label: SURVIVAL_JOB
choices.feedback: Rent paid. Most newcomers start in a survival job; the risk is staying there by default.

choices.text: Volunteer two days a week and go to every newcomer meetup and {faithHub} career night
choices.label: NETWORKING
choices.feedback: Most jobs are filled by referral. Volunteering gives you a Canadian reference.

choices.text: Only apply for jobs at your old level, and wait
choices.label: HOLDING_OUT

success.feedback: A callback, then an offer: your old level, a Canadian salary. It happens; just not often.
success.label: OLD_LEVEL_OFFER

fail.feedback: Forty more rejections. Savings drain faster than callbacks arrive.
fail.label: NO_CALLBACKS

FY_CREDENTIALS.title: The credential wall.
FY_CREDENTIALS.speaker: Settlement agency, Mississauga
FY_CREDENTIALS.dialogue: Your counsellor explains: regulated jobs (nursing, medicine, engineering, teaching, law) need a Canadian licence, often a year or two of assessments and exams. Unregulated jobs need a Canadian-style resume and a referral. Back home you were {occupation}.

choices.text: Enrol in a bridging program for internationally trained professionals, with a loan
choices.label: BRIDGING
choices.feedback: Slow and expensive, and the fastest legal way back to your profession.

choices.text: Take a PSW or assistant job in your field and study for the exams at night
choices.label: BRIDGE_JOB
choices.feedback: Paid, close to your field, exhausting. Many nurses spend their first years as PSWs.

choices.text: Unregulated field: rewrite your CV the Canadian way and get a cloud certification on weekends
choices.label: CERT_AND_CV
choices.feedback: Two pages, no photo, no date of birth, no state of origin. The certificate gets you past the robots.

choices.text: Drive Uber full-time and park the career for now
choices.label: PARKED_CAREER
choices.feedback: Good money this month. Credentials that sit unused get harder to restart.

FY_BLACK_TAX.title: {parent} is calling.
FY_BLACK_TAX.speaker: Your room, Brampton
FY_BLACK_TAX.dialogue: School fees for your sister, and Uncle's hospital bill: ₦1.2 million. The family sold land to send you; you know it, they know it, and nobody says it.

choices.text: Send all of it this week
choices.label: SENT_EVERYTHING
choices.feedback: Family happy, rent at risk. Black tax with no budget eats every pay cheque.

choices.text: Send a fixed share, about 15% of what you earn, every month, and explain the plan
choices.label: FIXED_SHARE
choices.feedback: Uncle's bill is still open. He'll mention it at the next family gathering. The plan holds anyway.

choices.text: Say no this time; you are not stable yet
choices.label: SAID_NO
choices.feedback: Silence on the family group for a week. You can feel it from here.

FY_WINTER.title: January.
FY_WINTER.speaker: Brampton
FY_WINTER.dialogue: −28°C with the wind. Dark at 4:45 p.m. You have not spoken to anyone in person in three days. Somebody in the group chat says 'Canada is not for the weak' with a laughing emoji. You are not laughing.

choices.text: Stay inside and scroll until spring
choices.label: HIBERNATED
choices.feedback: Seasonal low mood is common among newcomers, and isolation makes it worse.

choices.text: Join the Nigerian association's winter games night and the {faithGroup}
choices.label: FOUND_PEOPLE
choices.feedback: Community is the thing every newcomer says they underestimated.

choices.text: Visit a walk-in clinic or call 811 about your mood (covered by your health card)
choices.label: GOT_HELP
choices.feedback: Family doctors have waitlists. Walk-in clinics and 811 are how most newcomers start.

FY_WORK_EVENT.title: Month nine.
FY_WORK_EVENT.speaker: Mississauga
FY_WORK_EVENT.dialogue: Month nine. Work dries up: the contract ends early, or the app cuts your rate. 'Restructuring.' The job market has been rough for newcomers since 2024.

choices.text: Apply for Employment Insurance if you have the hours, and retrain
choices.label: EI_AND_RETRAIN
choices.feedback: EI needs enough insurable hours from a real employer. App gig work usually doesn't count. If you qualify, use the weeks well.

choices.text: Move to Calgary: cheaper rent, no provincial sales tax, and your field is hiring
choices.label: MOVED_PROVINCE
choices.feedback: Cheaper rent and a real job offer, far from everyone you know. {RelName} in {relCity} promises to visit.

choices.text: Take any shift on any app this week
choices.label: ANY_SHIFT
choices.feedback: Rent paid. The resume gap grows.

FY_DECEMBER.title: Detty December is calling.
FY_DECEMBER.speaker: Brampton
FY_DECEMBER.dialogue: Flights to {airportCode} are CAD 2,400. Your friends are posting countdowns. The IJGB ('I Just Got Back') season starts in two weeks. Someone asks if you are 'coming home for good'.

choices.text: Stay. Save for next year and keep building
choices.label: STAYED
choices.feedback: One quiet December, one step closer. Most first years end like this.

choices.text: Go home for December as an IJGB and spend big
choices.label: IJGB
choices.feedback: Jollof, owambe, your mother's face. And January's rent.

choices.text: Go home for good
choices.label: WENT_HOME

FY_FIELD.title: Back in your field.
FY_FIELD.speaker: Downtown Toronto
FY_FIELD.dialogue: A referral from someone you met at a potluck, a Canadian reference from your volunteering, a licence exam passed. The offer letter has your real job title on it.

outcome.title: Back in your field
outcome.subtitle: Year One done. Your career is moving again.
outcome.lesson: Credential recognition and the 'Canadian experience' gap take most skilled newcomers a year or more. Bridging programs, volunteering and referrals are what shorten it.

FY_SURVIVING.title: Surviving.
FY_SURVIVING.speaker: Brampton
FY_SURVIVING.dialogue: Rent paid, family helped, savings small but alive. Your career is on pause, not over. Year two is when people either climb or settle.

outcome.title: Surviving, not thriving
outcome.subtitle: You made it through Year One. Now plan the climb.
outcome.lesson: Statistics Canada finds immigrants with foreign degrees are about twice as likely to be overqualified for their jobs. Most climb out by planning it: licensing, bridging, networking.

FY_JAPADA.title: Japada.
FY_JAPADA.speaker: {airport}
FY_JAPADA.dialogue: You land at {airportCode}. The heat hits like a hug. The group chat says 'reverse japa' like it's a scandal. Your mother says nothing and cooks.

outcome.title: Reverse japa
outcome.subtitle: You went home. It is allowed.
outcome.lesson: About one in five immigrants leaves Canada within 25 years (Conference Board, 2025). Permanent residents must live in Canada two of every five years to keep PR; citizenship keeps both doors open.

FY_BURNOUT.title: Out of everything.
FY_BURNOUT.speaker: Brampton
FY_BURNOUT.dialogue: Money, sleep, patience: all gone at once. You call {relName}, who says the thing nobody said before you came: 'Everybody's first year is like this. Nobody posts it.'

outcome.title: Year One won
outcome.subtitle: Rest, then try again with help.
outcome.lesson: Newcomers in their first five years have had far higher unemployment than people born in Canada. Settlement agencies, food banks, EI and free counselling exist for the hard months; using them is not failure.

ST_REFUSED_AGAIN.title: Refused again.
ST_REFUSED_AGAIN.speaker: Your inbox
ST_REFUSED_AGAIN.dialogue: Same file, same officer reasoning, same two lines. Another application fee gone.
