outcome.title: Refused twice
outcome.subtitle: A refusal tells you what to fix. Fix it first.
outcome.lesson: Insufficient funds and 'not satisfied you will leave' are the most common reasons Nigerian study permits are refused. GCMS notes show the officer's actual reasoning; read them before you pay another fee.

ST_AGENT_SCAM.title: The agent's phone is off.
ST_AGENT_SCAM.speaker: {area}, {city}
ST_AGENT_SCAM.dialogue: The office is now a phone repair shop. The 'guaranteed visa' was a PDF. You are one of about forty people outside with the same receipt.

outcome.title: Scammed by a 'guaranteed visa'
outcome.subtitle: Nobody can guarantee a Canadian visa.
outcome.lesson: IRCC and the Nigeria Police warn that anyone promising a guaranteed visa is a scammer. Only lawyers and licensed consultants (check the CICC register) may charge for immigration advice.

ST_HOUSING.title: Where will you sleep?
ST_HOUSING.speaker: Brampton
ST_HOUSING.dialogue: Your residence application was waitlisted. A listing offers a bunk bed in a shared basement for CAD 375 with three post-dated cheques and no lease. A Nigerian church's student fellowship offers two weeks with a host family while you search.

choices.text: Two weeks with the church host family, then a proper room near campus
choices.label: HOST_FAMILY
choices.feedback: Jollof on day one, a lease on day twelve. Community networks meet students at the airport for a reason.

choices.text: Take the CAD 375 bunk bed: you are here to save money
choices.label: BUNK_BED
choices.feedback: Six people, one bathroom, one fire exit. Overcrowded basements are a known risk for international students.

choices.text: Pay a CAD 1,500 deposit to a Facebook landlord you haven't met
choices.label: RENTAL_SCAM
choices.feedback: He blocked you after the e-transfer. Never pay before a viewing.

EE_REFERENCE.title: Write it yourself.
EE_REFERENCE.speaker: Your old office, {city}
EE_REFERENCE.dialogue: Every job you claim needs a reference letter: dates, hours, salary and your real duties, on letterhead, signed. Your old company has shut down and your boss has relocated to Dubai. On WhatsApp he says: 'You know what you did. Write it and I'll sign.'

choices.text: Write your real duties in your own words and chase his signature from Dubai
choices.label: REAL_DUTIES

success.feedback: Signed and scanned from Dubai in four days. Your duties, your words.
success.label: SIGNED

fail.feedback: He's 'travelling'. You send payslips, tax records and a sworn statement instead: slower, DHL fees, still honest.
fail.label: SWORN_STATEMENT

choices.text: Copy the NOC duties word for word so it matches perfectly
choices.label: COPIED_NOC
choices.feedback: Officers know the NOC text by heart. A letter that reads exactly like it invites questions.

choices.text: Leave that job out to save time
choices.label: DROPPED_A_JOB
choices.feedback: Fewer points, and an employment history that doesn't match your earlier visa files.

EE_PFL.title: Procedural fairness letter.
EE_PFL.speaker: IRCC portal
EE_PFL.dialogue: 'We have concerns that the duties described in your reference letter were copied from the National Occupational Classification. You have 30 days to respond.' A PFL is not a refusal yet. It is a chance.

choices.text: Hire a licensed consultant or lawyer and send pay slips, tax records and a corrected letter in your own words
choices.label: ANSWERED_PFL
choices.feedback: Evidence that the job was real answered the concern.

choices.text: Ignore it and hope it goes away
choices.label: IGNORED_PFL

choices.text: Ask a 'connect' for a backdated 'clarification letter'
choices.label: FRAUD

EE_PFL_REFUSED.title: Refused.
EE_PFL_REFUSED.speaker: IRCC portal
EE_PFL_REFUSED.dialogue: Thirty days passed. The officer decided on the file as it was: refused. The invitation is gone; the pool is waiting again.

outcome.title: Refused after a PFL
outcome.subtitle: A procedural fairness letter is the officer asking for your side.
outcome.lesson: A PFL gives you a deadline (often 30 days) to answer a concern before a decision. Answering with real evidence often saves the file; silence almost never does.

TR_LMIA_SELLER.title: 'Positive LMIA, CAD 25k only.'
TR_LMIA_SELLER.speaker: WhatsApp, cousin's couch
TR_LMIA_SELLER.dialogue: He sends a PDF on old letterhead and a voice note: 'Calgary warehouse, approved LMIA, half now, half when you land the work permit.' Wey Sabi says his cousin did it.

choices.text: Send the CAD 1,500 'processing deposit' now; the rest when the permit lands
choices.label: PAID_FOR_LMIA

choices.text: Ask for the employer's legal name and the LMIA number, then check the company yourself
choices.label: VERIFIED
choices.feedback: He stopped replying after the second question. Workers never pay for an LMIA; the employer applies and pays the fee.

choices.text: Report the ad to the Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre and warn the family group chat
choices.label: REPORTED
choices.feedback: Two cousins thank you. One forwards it anyway.

TR_LMIA_PAID.title: The LMIA was never real.
TR_LMIA_PAID.speaker: WhatsApp
TR_LMIA_PAID.dialogue: The 'LMIA' number belongs to a bakery in Halifax. The agent's WhatsApp picture is now a sunset. Your savings went with it.

outcome.title: Paid for an LMIA
outcome.subtitle: Workers never pay for an LMIA.
outcome.lesson: Charging a worker for an LMIA or a job offer is illegal in Canada; the employer applies to ESDC and pays the CAD 1,000 fee. Since March 2025 a job offer adds no Express Entry points either.

KW_CAUGHT.title: A tip to CBSA.
KW_CAUGHT.speaker: Warehouse, Etobicoke
KW_CAUGHT.dialogue: A co-worker you argued with makes a call. Working without a permit while your claim is pending gets you a removal order and a very difficult conversation with your lawyer.

outcome.title: Caught working without a permit
outcome.subtitle: Wait for the permit. It usually comes.
outcome.lesson: Refugee claimants can get an open work permit once the claim is eligible and the medical is done. Working before that is unauthorized work, and enforcement often starts with a tip.

SUV_VANCE_TRACTION.speaker: Ms. Vance (Committee Chair)
SUV_VANCE_TRACTION.dialogue: Fine. Then show me traction. Who is paying you today, and how do I know they exist?

choices.text: Four paying pilots in Lagos and one Toronto importer, with signed letters of intent. Small, but real.
choices.label: REAL_TRACTION
choices.feedback: Small and verifiable beats big and vague. Committees call your references.

choices.text: 'Ten thousand active users.' (You have four hundred.)
choices.label: INFLATED_NUMBERS
choices.feedback: Ms. Vance asks for the analytics dashboard. Due diligence is the whole job.

choices.text: Book a live call with your biggest pilot customer right now
choices.label: CALL_THE_CUSTOMER

success.feedback: A Lagos shipper's logistics company picks up on the second ring and talks for four minutes about saved days.
success.label: CUSTOMER_PICKED_UP

fail.feedback: Voicemail. 'The number you are calling is switched off.' Ms. Vance writes something down.
fail.label: SWITCHED_OFF

SUV_VANCE_TRACTION.title: 'Show me traction.'

SUV_CHEN_DEMO.speaker: Dr. Chen (Chief Technology Officer)
SUV_CHEN_DEMO.dialogue: Share your screen. I'd like to see a settlement go through, live, start to finish.

choices.text: Run the live demo on your own laptop
choices.label: LIVE_DEMO

success.feedback: The settlement clears in 3.2 seconds. Dr. Chen unmutes just to say 'nice'.
success.label: DEMO_WORKED

fail.feedback: NEPA takes the light, the router reboots, the demo freezes at 'Processing…'. You narrate the rest from memory.
fail.label: NEPA_TOOK_THE_DEMO

choices.text: Play the pre-recorded walkthrough, and offer sandbox access after the call
choices.label: RECORDED_DEMO
choices.feedback: Safe and honest. Dr. Chen will try the sandbox tonight.

choices.text: Show the clickable Figma prototype and call it 'the live system'
choices.label: FAKE_DEMO
choices.feedback: Dr. Chen asks you to change one field. Figma doesn't do that.

SUV_CHEN_DEMO.title: Live demo?

SUV_ROSS_MONEY.speaker: Mr. Ross (Managing Partner)
SUV_ROSS_MONEY.dialogue: Last question. How long can you survive in Toronto before revenue, and who is putting money in besides you?

choices.text: Twelve months of runway plus the settlement funds IRCC wants, shown in naira and dollars
choices.label: REAL_RUNWAY
choices.feedback: Founders must show settlement funds of their own as well. You've planned for the naira slipping again.

choices.text: A Lagos angel will put in CAD 75,000 if you get the Letter
choices.label: ANGEL_PROMISE

success.feedback: The angel's term sheet is already in your data room. Ross reads it during the call.
success.label: TERM_SHEET_READY

fail.feedback: 'Conditional on the visa' plus 'no signed paper' sounds like 'no money' to Ross.
fail.label: VAPOUR_MONEY

choices.feedback: Only a designated Canadian angel group (CAD 75k+) or VC fund (CAD 200k+) counts. Your uncle's friend doesn't.

choices.text: Offer the incubator a ₦25 million 'fee' to guarantee the Letter
choices.label: PAY_TO_PLAY

SUV_ROSS_MONEY.title: Show me the money.

SUV_PAY_TO_PLAY.speaker: Mr. Ross (Managing Partner)
SUV_PAY_TO_PLAY.dialogue: The call goes quiet. 'We don't sell Letters of Support.' Two days later, a consultant who heard about your pitch offers to 'arrange one' for CAD 80,000.

outcome.title: Tried to buy a Letter of Support
outcome.subtitle: Designated organizations invest in businesses; they don't sell visas.
outcome.lesson: Pay-to-play schemes were one of the integrity concerns around the Startup Visa program. Designated organizations invest; they don't sell Letters of Support, and a bought letter can be found non-genuine, which is misrepresentation.

SUV_PAY_TO_PLAY.title: The call goes quiet.

LMIA_WAGE.speaker: Mr. Kovacs (Operations Director)
LMIA_WAGE.dialogue: Say we try. What salary are you expecting? Be honest; it changes the paperwork.

choices.text: The Job Bank median for this occupation in Peel Region, and I've brought the printout
choices.label: PREVAILING_WAGE
choices.feedback: An LMIA must offer at least the prevailing wage. You just did his homework.

choices.text: Accept a dollar below the median if he signs this week
choices.label: LOWBALL
choices.feedback: It sounds smart. Service Canada refuses offers below the prevailing wage, and it looks desperate.

choices.text: Ask for well above the median: you're worth it
choices.label: HIGH_ASK
choices.feedback: The prevailing wage is the floor, not the target. Overshooting makes him rethink the whole thing.

LMIA_WAGE.title: The wage question.

LMIA_FEE_ASK.speaker: Mr. Kovacs (Operations Director)
LMIA_FEE_ASK.dialogue: Last thing. Our lawyer's quote is CAD 6,000 plus the CAD 1,000 government fee. Some companies have the worker cover that. Would you?

choices.text: Explain, politely, that employers can't recover LMIA costs from workers, and offer to save him the hours instead
choices.label: KNOWS_THE_RULES
choices.feedback: Recovering LMIA fees from a worker is prohibited. Kovacs didn't know; his lawyer confirms it.

choices.text: Pay it: CAD 7,000, half now from your savings
choices.label: PAID_FOR_IT

choices.text: Ask if he can pay you cash while the LMIA processes
choices.label: CASH_ASK

LMIA_FEE_ASK.title: Who pays?

LMIA_WORKER_PAID.speaker: Northline Logistics
LMIA_WORKER_PAID.dialogue: Three months later an ESDC inspection finds your e-transfer. The employer broke the rules by taking it: the LMIA is revoked and the company is fined. You can report it and ask for your money back, but this job is gone.

outcome.title: The employer made you pay
outcome.subtitle: Employers can't recover LMIA costs from workers.
outcome.lesson: Employers can't recover LMIA costs from workers. If one does, the employer is at fault: the LMIA can be revoked and the employer fined or banned, and the worker can report it to ESDC's tip line.

LMIA_WORKER_PAID.title: The inspection.

LMIA_CASH.speaker: Mr. Kovacs
LMIA_CASH.dialogue: Kovacs's face changes. 'I can't do that, and I'm a little worried you asked.' The meeting ends.

outcome.title: Asked for cash work
outcome.subtitle: Visitors can't work, even 'just until the papers come'.
outcome.lesson: Working on a visitor record is unauthorized work, and an employer who pays cash risks fines and a ban from the program. Asking for it costs you the employer's trust.

LMIA_CASH.title: The cash question.

ST_SPOUSE.title: 'When am I coming?'
ST_SPOUSE.speaker: WhatsApp video call
ST_SPOUSE.dialogue: Your partner back home asks the question every week. Since January 2025, a spouse gets an open work permit only if you're in a master's of 16 months or more, a PhD, or certain professional programs. Your program decides what's possible.

choices.text: Apply for your spouse's open work permit: your 16-month master's qualifies
choices.label: SPOUSAL_OWP
choices.feedback: Approved. Two incomes, one basement, half the loneliness.
choices.lockedHint: Only for master's (16+ months), PhD or some professional programs

choices.text: Apply for a visitor visa so they can at least visit
choices.label: SPOUSE_VISIT

success.feedback: Approved for a visit. Three weeks of jollof and hugs in January.
success.label: VISIT_APPROVED

fail.feedback: Refused: 'not satisfied they will leave Canada'. Spouses of students hear that a lot.
fail.label: VISIT_REFUSED

choices.text: Agree to wait: you'll apply together once you have a PGWP
choices.label: WAIT_FOR_PGWP
choices.feedback: Honest and hard. Video calls at 6 a.m. Toronto time, noon in {city}.

TR_CAREGIVER_AD.title: 'Caregiver sponsorship, limited slots.'
TR_CAREGIVER_AD.speaker: Facebook, cousin's couch
TR_CAREGIVER_AD.dialogue: ₦600,000 for 'training and placement', then a Canadian family sponsors you. Wey Sabi says caregiver na the easy route.

choices.text: Pay the training fee before the slots fill
choices.label: PAID_CAREGIVER_FEE

choices.text: Check IRCC's page for the home care worker pilots first
choices.label: VERIFIED
choices.feedback: The home care worker pilots filled their caps on day one in 2025 and aren't open to new applications right now. The ad is selling a closed door.

choices.text: Report the page and warn the family group chat
choices.label: REPORTED
choices.feedback: Somebody's aunty was about to pay. She thanks you with a voice note.

TR_CAREGIVER_PAID.title: Training complete. Placement: never.
TR_CAREGIVER_PAID.speaker: Facebook
TR_CAREGIVER_PAID.dialogue: You got a certificate with a gold border and a WhatsApp group that went silent. The 'sponsoring family' was never real.

outcome.title: Paid for a closed door
outcome.subtitle: The caregiver pilots aren't open, and no family sells sponsorship.
outcome.lesson: Canada's home care worker pilots reached their caps on day one in March 2025 and are not taking new applications. Check that a program is open on canada.ca before paying anyone.

FY_ACCENT.title: 'Can you speak slower?'
FY_ACCENT.speaker: Your new team, Mississauga
FY_ACCENT.dialogue: Team meeting, week three. Your manager stops you mid-update: 'Can you speak slower? Your accent…' Two people look at their shoes. You've spoken English your whole life.

choices.text: Keep going, a little slower, and send a crisp written summary after
choices.label: LET_IT_SLIDE
choices.feedback: Your written summary becomes the one everyone forwards. The comment still stings.

choices.text: Ask your manager for a quick chat after: what exactly was unclear?
choices.label: NAMED_IT

success.feedback: She apologises: 'That came out wrong.' The next meeting, she asks for your view first.
success.label: MANAGER_LISTENED

fail.feedback: 'Don't be so sensitive.' You note the date in your phone, just in case.
fail.label: BRUSHED_OFF

choices.text: Join the company's Black employee network and find a mentor
choices.label: FOUND_A_MENTOR
choices.feedback: A senior director from home takes you to lunch. 'I heard the same thing in 2009. Here's what I did.'

LAGOS_AGENT_SCAM.title: 'Your file is moving.'
LAGOS_AGENT_SCAM.speaker: Agent's office, {city}
LAGOS_AGENT_SCAM.dialogue: Two weeks later the office has a new signboard and his number is switched off. Nobody 'knows people'. Nobody can make an IRCC file move faster.

outcome.title: Facilitation fee, gone
outcome.subtitle: There is no fast lane for sale.
outcome.lesson: Only CICC-licensed consultants, lawyers and Quebec notaries may charge to help with an application. Check the public register. Nobody can pay IRCC to speed up a file.

NURSE_VERIFY.title: Matron knows.
NURSE_VERIFY.speaker: Nurses' station, {area}, 2 a.m.
NURSE_VERIFY.dialogue: Matron drops the roster. 'Three of you resigned this month. If you request council verification, I go know say you dey go.' Your colleague's letter took four months.

choices.text: Apply quietly to the nursing council and keep doing nights
choices.label: QUIET_VERIFY
choices.feedback: Verification goes from the council straight to the Canadian assessor: NNAS for most provinces, while BC's college assesses you directly. Slow, but clean.

choices.text: Tell Matron and ask for a reference letter
choices.label: TOLD_MATRON

success.feedback: She's hurt. She still signs: 'the best I've trained'. You'll need that letter.
success.label: MATRON_SIGNED

fail.feedback: She signs, slowly, and moves you to permanent nights 'since you're leaving anyway'.
fail.label: PERMANENT_NIGHTS

choices.text: Pay a 'man at the council' ₦300k to fast-track it
choices.label: COUNCIL_TOUT

NURSE_TOUT.title: The fast lane was a man with a POS.
NURSE_TOUT.speaker: Outside the council office
NURSE_TOUT.dialogue: He collected cash, sent a 'tracking number', and blocked you. Your real verification request never left the building.

outcome.title: Paid the 'man at the council'
outcome.subtitle: There is no fast lane for sale.
outcome.lesson: Nursing verification goes from the council to the Canadian assessor (NNAS for most provinces; BC's college assesses directly), and the provincial college decides when you sit the NCLEX-RN. Nobody sells a shortcut; touts sell receipts.

NURSE_UK_OR_CANADA.title: 'Come UK first, babe.'
NURSE_UK_OR_CANADA.speaker: WhatsApp, after your night shift
NURSE_UK_OR_CANADA.dialogue: Your set mate Ngozi voice-notes from Manchester: 'CBT, OSCE, I land in eight months. Come UK first, Canada later.' Your Canadian assessment has been 'in review' for a year. Canada pays more. UK is faster.

choices.text: Stay the Canada course: finish the assessment and wait for the provincial college to clear you for the NCLEX-RN
choices.label: NCLEX
choices.feedback: Assessment first (NNAS, or BC's college directly), then the provincial regulator decides when you can write the NCLEX-RN. Express Entry PR alone doesn't make you an RN in Canada; the licence does.

choices.text: Enter the Express Entry pool now and sort the licence after you land
choices.label: POOL_FIRST
choices.feedback: Legal and common. Just budget for months of PSW or assistant work while the college processes you.

choices.text: Go UK first; Canada can wait
choices.label: UK_FIRST

NURSE_UK.title: Manchester, eight months later.
NURSE_UK.speaker: Manchester Airport
NURSE_UK.dialogue: You japa'd, just not to Canada. Ngozi meets you at arrivals with a Greggs sausage roll. The Canada file sleeps in your Drive.

outcome.title: Japa'd to the UK
outcome.subtitle: Not Canada, but out. Many nurses do UK first.
outcome.lesson: Many Nigerian nurses go UK first. Moving on to Canada later means Canadian licensing: an assessment (NNAS, or BC's college directly), then the NCLEX-RN when the provincial college clears you. Keep your documents.

TR_CASH_SHIFT.title: Shift starts 6, cash at 2.
TR_CASH_SHIFT.speaker: Warehouse lot, Bolton
TR_CASH_SHIFT.dialogue: Agency man: 'No SIN, no wahala. CAD 14 an hour, cash.' That's below Ontario's CAD 17.60 minimum wage, and you'd have no one to complain to. Your wallet says what it says.

choices.text: Do the shift. Just one.
choices.label: CASH_SHIFT

choices.text: Decline, and take the free resume clinic at the library instead
choices.label: DECLINED_CASH
choices.feedback: Slower money. Zero risk to your record.

choices.text: Help at the {faithHub} for a plate of food and some contacts
choices.label: VOLUNTEERED
choices.feedback: Volunteering is allowed. The aunty serving rice knows a hiring manager.

TR_CASH_CAUGHT.title: The van, the inspector, your name.
TR_CASH_CAUGHT.speaker: Warehouse lot, Bolton
TR_CASH_CAUGHT.dialogue: The inspector is polite. The questions are not. A visitor working without a permit is reported to CBSA.

outcome.title: Caught working on a visitor record
outcome.subtitle: One shift, one inspection.
outcome.lesson: Visitors can look for work and attend interviews but cannot work. Unauthorized work can lead to a removal order and makes every future visa harder.

TR_COUCH_TIGHT.title: The couch gets small.
TR_COUCH_TIGHT.speaker: Cousin's flat, Brampton
TR_COUCH_TIGHT.dialogue: Month three. Your cousin's wife doesn't greet again. 'Ẹ̀gbọ́n, the kids need the parlour for homework.' Your cousin stares at his phone.

choices.text: Offer CAD 300 a month 'for light'
choices.label: PAID_FOR_LIGHT
choices.feedback: She greets you the next morning. Money talks, even in Brampton.

choices.text: Move to a {faithHub} member's basement
choices.label: MOVED_OUT
choices.feedback: Smaller room, bigger network. Your cousin helps carry the box, relieved.

choices.text: Pretend not to notice
choices.label: IGNORED_IT
choices.feedback: Yoruba people don't shout. They go cold.

TR_GO_HOME.title: Return ticket.
TR_GO_HOME.speaker: Toronto Pearson, Departures
TR_GO_HOME.dialogue: No LMIA, no lies, no overstay. Your cousin hugs you and pushes CAD 100 into your pocket. 'Come back the right way.'

outcome.title: Clean record, next time stronger
outcome.subtitle: You leave on time. That counts for more than people think.
outcome.lesson: Leaving before your visitor status ends keeps your travel history clean. A Canadian network, savings and a compliant record make your next application stronger.

SUV_COMPLIANCE.title: One more thing.
SUV_COMPLIANCE.speaker: Ms. Vance (Committee Chair)
SUV_COMPLIANCE.dialogue: You move money across borders. Who regulates you in Canada?

choices.text: We register with FINTRAC as a money services business and budget for a compliance officer
choices.label: FINTRAC
choices.feedback: The right answer, and an expensive one. Payments in Canada are regulated.

choices.text: Our Nigerian licence covers us
choices.label: WRONG_LICENCE
choices.feedback: Licences don't cross borders.

choices.text: We'll sort regulation after we scale
choices.label: LATER
choices.feedback: Every investor on this call has seen a fintech die of 'later'.

FY_GIG_LIFE.title: 4.71 stars.
FY_GIG_LIFE.speaker: Driver's seat, Mississauga
FY_GIG_LIFE.dialogue: The app dropped your rating after a passenger complained you 'talked too much'. Below 4.7 you get deactivated. Gas is up. The car payment is not going anywhere.

choices.text: Keep driving, keep quiet, chase the airport runs
choices.label: KEEP_DRIVING
choices.feedback: The money is real. The career is still parked.

choices.text: Drive mornings only, and use evenings for a certificate
choices.label: SPLIT_TIME
choices.feedback: Less money, a way out.

choices.text: Ask the Naija drivers' WhatsApp group how they stay above 4.8
choices.label: ASKED_DRIVERS
choices.feedback: Phone charger, water bottles, no politics. And Calgary drivers say the rent there is half.

FY_TAXES.title: First tax season.
FY_TAXES.speaker: Volunteer tax clinic
FY_TAXES.dialogue: April. A coworker asks if you've filed. Filed what? A friend of a cousin in the group chat 'does taxes': he promises a CAD 4,000 refund and charges 20% of it.

choices.text: Use a free community volunteer tax clinic
choices.label: TAX_CLINIC
choices.feedback: Filing, even on small income, unlocks the GST/HST credit and other benefits newcomers miss.

choices.text: Let the group-chat guy claim expenses you don't have
choices.label: FAKE_EXPENSES

choices.text: Skip it: you barely earned anything
choices.label: SKIPPED_TAXES
choices.feedback: Not filing means missing credits you're owed, and it can slow down your PR or citizenship paperwork later.

FY_TAX_FAIL.title: The CRA letter.
FY_TAX_FAIL.speaker: Your mailbox
FY_TAX_FAIL.dialogue: Eight months later: a reassessment. The expenses were invented, the refund is clawed back with interest and a penalty, and the 'tax guy' has changed his number.

outcome.title: Refund today, CRA tomorrow
outcome.subtitle: The group-chat tax guy has a new number.
outcome.lesson: False claims on a tax return are fraud: the CRA reassesses, charges penalties and interest, and you are responsible for what your preparer files. Free volunteer clinics exist for low-income newcomers.

FY_SILENCE.title: {parent} hasn't called in three weeks.
FY_SILENCE.speaker: WhatsApp, Sunday night
FY_SILENCE.dialogue: You said no in the spring. Uncle's bill got paid by your cousin in Houston, and everyone knows it. {parent}'s last message is a forwarded prayer with no greeting.

choices.text: Call first. Explain the year honestly, and send something small
choices.label: MADE_PEACE
choices.feedback: 'My child, why didn't you tell me it was this hard?'

choices.text: Wait for them to call you
choices.label: WAITED
choices.feedback: Pride on both sides. December is going to be awkward.

FY_CUSTOMS.title: Ghana Must Go.
FY_CUSTOMS.speaker: Toronto Pearson, customs
FY_CUSTOMS.dialogue: {parent} packed {homeFood}. The kiosk asks: 'Bringing food?' The man behind you whispers, 'Tick No. Dem no dey check.'

choices.text: Declare everything
choices.label: DECLARED
choices.feedback: The officer took the meat and waved the rest through. Declaring is how you avoid a fine.

choices.text: Tick No and walk
choices.label: UNDECLARED

success.feedback: Nobody stopped you. Your heart rate takes an hour to come down.
success.label: WALKED_THROUGH

fail.feedback: The beagle found the {homeMeat}. Undeclared food means a fine and a note on your record.
fail.label: BEAGLE

ST_SILENCE.title: PPR don land. Who do you tell?
ST_SILENCE.speaker: Family WhatsApp group
ST_SILENCE.dialogue: Your thumb hovers over the family group. {parent} says, 'Tell only God and me.' Your bestie wants to post your farewell with a photo of your boarding pass.

choices.text: Tell close family only, and japa in silence
choices.label: QUIET_JAPA
choices.feedback: Quiet japa: a Naija tradition. Nobody's village people get the memo.

choices.text: Announce it in the family group
choices.label: ANNOUNCED
choices.feedback: Contributions came in. So did fourteen shopping lists and an aunty who wants you to carry a 23 kg bag of garri.

choices.text: Let her post the boarding pass
choices.label: POSTED_PASS
choices.feedback: Two hundred likes. Never post a boarding pass or visa page: the barcode and numbers are personal data scammers love.

FY_FAITH.title: Every {faithDay}.
FY_FAITH.speaker: Your new schedule
FY_FAITH.dialogue: The schedule for your new job or program arrives. You're down for every {faithDay}, all month. {parent} asked on the phone last night if you've found a {faithHub} yet.

choices.text: Ask your supervisor, in writing, for a schedule change for religious reasons
choices.label: ASKED_ACCOMMODATION

success.feedback: Done in a day. Employers must accommodate religious practice up to undue hardship, and most do it quietly.
success.label: ACCOMMODATED

fail.feedback: 'We'll see.' Nothing changes for three weeks, then HR fixes it after you follow up. Stressful, but on record.
fail.label: SLOW_HR

choices.text: Swap shifts with a coworker who wants your weekday
choices.label: SWAPPED
choices.feedback: Informal, fast, and now you owe Priya a favour.

choices.text: Say nothing and skip {faithDay} for now
choices.label: SKIPPED_FAITH
choices.feedback: Your record is spotless. Your weeks feel longer.

ST_SCAM_CALL.title: 'This is IRCC.'
ST_SCAM_CALL.speaker: Unknown number, week one
ST_SCAM_CALL.dialogue: 'Your study permit has an error. Pay CAD 900 in gift cards today or you will be deported.' He knows your flight number and your seat. Your bestie's post had both.

choices.text: Hang up and check your IRCC account yourself
choices.label: HUNG_UP
choices.feedback: Nothing wrong. IRCC never phones to demand payment, and never in gift cards. You delete the post.

choices.text: Pay. You can't risk deportation in week one
choices.label: PAID_SCAMMER
choices.feedback: The number stops working an hour later. The post that started it still has 200 likes.

SUV_COFOUNDER.title: Between rounds.
SUV_COFOUNDER.speaker: Home office, Lekki, midnight
SUV_COFOUNDER.dialogue: The committee breaks until tomorrow. At midnight your CTO Dayo calls: a Manchester fintech offered him £70k and a visa. 'Guy, I no fit wait for Canada forever.' Mr. Ross asks about the team next.

choices.text: Give him 5% more equity and a seat on the founders' agreement
choices.label: MORE_EQUITY
choices.feedback: He stays. Your own share is smaller, and the cap table finally looks like a team.

choices.text: Ask him to give you two weeks: the Letter decides
choices.label: TWO_WEEKS

success.feedback: 'Two weeks. Then I'm gone.' He joins the call tomorrow and answers Mr. Ross himself.
success.label: DAYO_STAYS

fail.feedback: He signs with Manchester on Monday and sends you his notes. 'No vex.'
fail.label: DAYO_LEFT

choices.text: Let him go and promote Kemi, the junior dev who built the queue
choices.label: PROMOTED_KEMI
choices.feedback: Kemi is brilliant and terrified. The committee will ask about her experience.

NURSE_TWO_TESTS.title: Two tests, one nurse.
NURSE_TWO_TESTS.speaker: IELTS centre, {city}
NURSE_TWO_TESTS.dialogue: Your provincial nursing college sets its own English test. Ontario's accepts IELTS General or Academic, or CELBAN; BC's wants IELTS Academic, CELBAN or OET. Express Entry takes IELTS General, CELPIP or PTE Core, never Academic. The group chat argues about it for 300 messages.

choices.text: Write both: IELTS Academic for the college, PTE Core for Express Entry
choices.label: BOTH_TESTS
choices.feedback: Two receipts, two score reports, zero confusion later. Each one does a different job.

choices.text: Write only IELTS Academic and hope it covers both
choices.label: ONE_TEST
choices.feedback: The college is happy. Express Entry isn't: Academic doesn't count there, so you'll be booking again.

choices.text: Applying to Ontario: write IELTS General once, which the college and Express Entry both accept
choices.label: ONE_TEST
choices.feedback: One test, two uses. Check each one's minimum bands before you book.

TR_KUNLE.title: Kunle paid.
TR_KUNLE.speaker: Tim Hortons, Queen St, Brampton
TR_KUNLE.dialogue: Kunle slides his phone over: a CAD 28,000 receipt. 'The job was real for two weeks. Now the boss holds my passport and pays half. Abeg, no talk am for anybody.'

choices.text: Tell him about the open work permit for vulnerable workers, and help him find a settlement worker
choices.label: HELPED_KUNLE
choices.feedback: Holding someone's passport is illegal. Workers on an employer-specific permit who face abuse can apply for an open work permit. Kunle is a victim, not a criminal.

choices.text: Ask for his agent's number. Maybe yours will be different
choices.label: WANTED_AGENT

choices.text: Buy him a double-double and change the topic
choices.label: CHANGED_TOPIC
choices.feedback: He texts 'thanks' at 2 a.m. You don't reply.

AR_PITCH.title: The Agent Room.
AR_PITCH.speaker: Alhaji (Travel Consultant)
AR_PITCH.dialogue: 'Ah, my brother! You are in luck. A wealthy family in Calgary needs an urgent nanny. They already have an approved LMIA. No IELTS, no experience. Just pay ₦4.5M and you land in Canada in 4 weeks. Guaranteed.'

choices.text: 'Wow, 4 weeks? That is exactly what I need! Where do I make the deposit?'
choices.label: EAGER
choices.feedback: Red flag meter +1. He smiles like a man who has seen this movie.

choices.text: 'An approved LMIA? Give me the LMIA number and the employer's legal name so I can verify it.'
choices.label: ASKED_LMIA_NUMBER
choices.feedback: Skepticism +1. Real job offers come with a real employer you can check.

choices.text: 'No IELTS for a caregiver stream? I thought IRCC requires a minimum language level.'
choices.label: KNEW_THE_RULE
choices.feedback: Skepticism +1.5. The home care worker pilots require a language test (CLB 4) and they're not taking new applications.

AR_EAGER.title: 'Smart man!'
AR_EAGER.speaker: Alhaji (Travel Consultant)
AR_EAGER.dialogue: 'You see? You are serious. Pay the ₦1.5M commitment fee today, the rest when the visa comes. Someone from Abuja wants this slot.' He slides an account number across the desk. It's a personal account.

choices.text: Borrow from three loan apps and transfer the ₦1.5M today
choices.label: PAID_COMMITMENT

choices.text: Pause. 'Let me see the job offer letter and verify the employer first.'
choices.label: LATE_DOUBT
choices.feedback: Late, but not too late.

AR_PUSHBACK.title: 'Trust the process.'
AR_PUSHBACK.speaker: Alhaji (Travel Consultant)
AR_PUSHBACK.dialogue: He frowns, shuffling papers. 'Why are you asking for the number? That is proprietary. You will bypass me and steal the job. I have sent over 50 Nigerians this year. If you don't pay ₦1.5M commitment today, someone else takes the slot.'

choices.text: 'Okay, sorry sir. I don't want to lose the slot.' Transfer the ₦1.5M
choices.label: PAID_COMMITMENT

choices.text: 'No upfront fee without a job offer I can verify myself. Canadian employers pay the LMIA costs, not the applicant.'
choices.label: SAFE_ESCAPE

choices.text: 'Can we sign a legally binding contract drafted by my lawyer before any money moves?'
choices.label: LAWYER_CONTRACT

AR_SAFE.title: Scam avoided!
AR_SAFE.speaker: Outside the office, Ikeja
AR_SAFE.dialogue: He tells you to leave if you don't trust him. You do, gladly. Real LMIAs can't be bought or sold, a real offer names the employer, and applicants never pay the employer's LMIA fee.

choices.text: Walk to the bus stop with your ₦4.5M plan still in your pocket
choices.label: WALKED_AWAY
choices.feedback: Street Cred +20. Stress −10. Funds unchanged.

AR_RETALIATION.title: Agent retaliation.
AR_RETALIATION.speaker: Facebook, that evening
AR_RETALIATION.dialogue: Alhaji blocks you, then posts your photo in the group as 'a time waster who wants free things'. Three people message you privately: 'Thank you. He took my sister's money.'

choices.text: Report the page, then start your own file the honest way
choices.label: REPORTED_AGENT
choices.feedback: Embarrassing for a day. Your money is safe, and you warned three families.

AR_SCAM.title: 'Visa Approval.'
AR_SCAM.speaker: Murtala Muhammed Airport, Lagos
AR_SCAM.dialogue: Two weeks later Alhaji hands you a printed 'Visa Approval' letter. At check-in, the airline system can't find it. The letter was made in Photoshop. Alhaji has blocked your number.

outcome.title: Section 40: misrepresentation
outcome.subtitle: Alhaji has blocked your number on WhatsApp.
outcome.lesson: LMIAs can't be bought. Fake job offers and fake approvals are scams, and submitting a fake document to IRCC is misrepresentation under section 40 of IRPA: refusal and a five-year ban. Verify the employer and the LMIA yourself.

LAGOS_OGA.title: Oga at the top.
LAGOS_OGA.speaker: Your office, {area}
LAGOS_OGA.dialogue: Biometrics is Thursday, 10 a.m., in {vacCity}. Your manager approves leave only for 'death or wedding', and he checks the office WhatsApp group every 20 minutes.

choices.text: Ask HR for a day's leave in writing, and a letter confirming your job
choices.label: ASKED_HR

success.feedback: Approved. HR's letter confirms your role, salary and return date: real home ties for a visitor visa.
success.label: LEAVE_LETTER

fail.feedback: Approved, but Oga makes you 'cover' Saturday. No letter yet.
fail.label: WORK_SATURDAY

choices.text: Sneak out at lunch and be back before 2 p.m.
choices.label: SNEAKED_OUT

success.feedback: Back at 1:58 with suya for the team. Nobody asks.
success.label: CLEAN_ESCAPE

fail.feedback: Surprise meeting at 12:30. A query letter is waiting on your desk.
fail.label: QUERY_LETTER

choices.text: Call in sick. Malaria, the national excuse
choices.label: CALLED_IN_SICK

success.feedback: 'Get well soon.' You feel guilty for about four minutes.
success.label: GOT_AWAY

fail.feedback: A colleague posts your visa-centre selfie on her status. HR saw it. Final warning.
fail.label: STATUS_SNITCH

LAGOS_PASSPORT_TOUT.title: 'Tomorrow. Trust me.'
LAGOS_PASSPORT_TOUT.speaker: Passport office gate, {city}
LAGOS_PASSPORT_TOUT.dialogue: Tomorrow becomes next week. The booklet he finally brings has your photo and someone else's NIN. The real queue was inside, with the official fee and a receipt.

outcome.title: The tout's passport
outcome.subtitle: Your money, and maybe your identity, are gone.
outcome.lesson: Apply through the Nigeria Immigration Service's official portal and pay the official fee. Touts sell delays and fakes, and travelling on a passport with false details is document fraud everywhere.

LAGOS_JIJI.title: Tokunbo, first body.
LAGOS_JIJI.speaker: Car park, {area}
LAGOS_JIJI.dialogue: A buyer agrees ₦4.2M, no haggling. His phone buzzes; he shows you an SMS: 'Credit Alert: ₦4,200,000.00'. 'Oya, give me the keys and papers, I have another meeting.'

choices.text: Hand over the keys. The alert is right there
choices.label: FAKE_ALERT

choices.text: 'Let me check my bank app first.' Make him wait
choices.label: CHECKED_APP

success.feedback: Your app shows the money. You sign a sale agreement: a paper trail for your proof of funds.
success.label: SOLD_PROPERLY

fail.feedback: Nothing in the app. He 'remembers' a meeting and drives off in his friend's car. Your Corolla stays.
fail.label: BUYER_VANISHED

choices.text: Meet only at the police-station car park, bank to bank, for a lower price
choices.label: SAFE_SALE
choices.feedback: Slower and ₦300k cheaper. The money is real and the sale agreement is stamped.

LAGOS_JIJI_SCAM.title: Fake alert.
LAGOS_JIJI_SCAM.speaker: Car park, {area}
LAGOS_JIJI_SCAM.dialogue: Your bank app never moves. The 'alert' was an SMS anyone can send. The Corolla is already on the Third Mainland Bridge.

outcome.title: Fake credit alert
outcome.subtitle: The car is gone and so is your proof of funds.
outcome.lesson: Fake credit alerts are an old Lagos trick: an SMS proves nothing. Confirm money in your own bank app before you hand over anything, and keep a signed sale agreement: it's also how you show where your funds came from.

ST_FAMILY_MEETING.title: The family meeting.
ST_FAMILY_MEETING.speaker: {uncle}'s parlour
ST_FAMILY_MEETING.dialogue: Malt on the table, everyone in their seats. {uncle} clears his throat. An aunty asks, 'When you reach there, you go remember us?' A cousin says nothing very loudly.

choices.text: Present a budget sheet and promise a fixed monthly remittance once you're working
choices.label: PLEDGED
choices.feedback: Gift deeds signed, source of funds documented. The family group now expects updates.

choices.text: Ask {uncle} privately for a written gift deed with his bank statements
choices.label: PRIVATE_ASK

success.feedback: He signs a gift deed and gives you six months of statements. Clean, documented, quiet.
success.label: GIFT_DEED

fail.feedback: 'Next year.' By Sunday, everybody knows you asked.
fail.label: NEXT_YEAR

choices.text: Ask for a loan you'll repay double once you land
choices.label: FAMILY_LOAN
choices.feedback: A loan isn't a gift. Officers ask whether funds must be repaid, and a big debt weakens your file.

ST_CROWDFUND.title: Go viral or go home.
ST_CROWDFUND.speaker: Your phone, ring light on
ST_CROWDFUND.dialogue: One video, your whole future. Too dramatic and X will drag you. Too boring and nobody donates.

choices.text: Honest video: admission letter, grades, budget, receipts
choices.label: HONEST_CROWDFUND
choices.feedback: Modest, steady donations. People trust receipts.

choices.text: Dramatic video: tears, slow music, 'my last hope'
choices.label: DRAMATIC_CROWDFUND

success.feedback: It goes viral. CAD 9,000 in a weekend, and 400 new followers who want updates.
success.label: WENT_VIRAL

fail.feedback: Someone finds your brunch photos from last month. The quote-tweets are brutal.
fail.label: DRAGGED

choices.text: Delete the draft. Pride
choices.label: NO_CROWDFUND

ST_FX.title: The rate moved again.
ST_FX.speaker: Bureau de change, {city}
ST_FX.dialogue: Your tuition deposit is due in Canadian dollars. The parallel market jumped this week, and every day your naira buys less.

choices.text: Convert now through your bank, with receipts
choices.label: CONVERTED_NOW
choices.feedback: A bad rate, but documented: receipts are part of your proof of funds.

choices.text: Wait one more week for the rate to calm down
choices.label: WAITED_FX

success.feedback: The naira steadies. You convert CAD 2,500 better off.
success.label: RATE_EASED

fail.feedback: It slides another 12%. Your buffer shrinks by CAD 4,500.
fail.label: RATE_CRASHED

choices.text: Top up the gap with an instant loan app
choices.label: LOAN_APP
choices.feedback: 30% a month, and they text your contacts the day you're late. It's legal-ish. It's also a trap.

ST_REVIEW_1.title: The officer opens your file.
ST_REVIEW_1.speaker: Visa officer (file review)
ST_REVIEW_1.dialogue: Typing, fast, barely looking up. 'Study permit. Why this specific program, and why now?' Canada rarely interviews study-permit applicants: the officer 'asks' by reading your file. Answer the way your documents would.

choices.text: 'The economy in Nigeria is bad, and Canada has great opportunities for international students.'
choices.label: CLICHE
choices.feedback: Every refused file says this. It explains why you want to leave, not why this program.

choices.text: 'This program adds a specialization my degree doesn't have, and it builds directly on {sopBackground}.'
choices.label: ACADEMIC_PITCH
choices.feedback: A logical career step. The officer stops typing.

choices.text: Freeze. Say nothing useful
choices.label: FROZE_1
choices.feedback: Your study plan left that question blank.

ST_REVIEW_2.title: 'Where did this money come from?'
ST_REVIEW_2.speaker: Visa officer (file review)
ST_REVIEW_2.dialogue: 'I see a lump sum of ₦15,000,000 deposited three weeks ago. Where did these funds come from?'

choices.text: 'My uncle pooled it from his friends to meet the requirement. I'll return it when I land.'
choices.label: POOLED_FUNDS
choices.feedback: Honest, but fatal to the file: money you must give back isn't yours to study on. Borrowed or pooled funds don't count.

choices.text: 'A gift deed from my mother, from the sale of her shop, with the sale deed and tax receipts on page 14.'
choices.label: PAPER_TRAIL
choices.feedback: Clear, verifiable origin. The officer nods slowly.

choices.text: Freeze
choices.label: FROZE_2
choices.feedback: A big recent deposit with no explanation is the classic refusal reason.

ST_REVIEW_3.title: 'What brings you back?'
ST_REVIEW_3.speaker: Visa officer (file review)
ST_REVIEW_3.dialogue: 'Everything is in order on paper. But you're young, single and selling assets. What brings you back to Nigeria after your program?'

choices.text: 'My whole family is here! I love Nigeria, my parents are old, I have to come back.'
choices.label: EMOTIONAL_TIES
choices.feedback: Sincere, and weak on its own. Officers weigh things they can verify.

choices.text: Your employer's signed study-leave letter, with a senior role waiting when you return
choices.label: STUDY_LEAVE
choices.feedback: A verifiable tie. The strongest answer, if it's real.
choices.lockedHint: Only if you really have a job to go back to

choices.text: 'I may apply to stay after graduating, legally. If I return, this is the career I'd build here.'
choices.label: DUAL_INTENT_HONEST
choices.feedback: Dual intent is allowed: wanting to stay later is fine if you'd follow the rules either way.

choices.text: Freeze
choices.label: FROZE_3
choices.feedback: Silence reads as no plan.

ST_PROF_EMAIL.title: The cold email.
ST_PROF_EMAIL.speaker: Your laptop, 2 a.m.
ST_PROF_EMAIL.dialogue: Funded research master's in Canada usually start with a professor who agrees to supervise you. Most applicants never get a reply. Your draft is open.

choices.text: Tailored: three lines on their 2024 paper, your thesis data, one clear question
choices.label: TAILORED_EMAIL

success.feedback: 'Interesting. Send your CV and transcript.' A professor in Edmonton replied.
success.label: PROF_REPLIED

fail.feedback: Silence. You send five more tailored emails over two weeks.
fail.label: NO_REPLY

choices.text: Mass-mail 200 professors: 'Dear Sir/Ma, I am interested in your esteemed research'
choices.label: MASS_EMAIL
choices.feedback: Straight to the trash folder. Generic emails are the easiest to ignore.

choices.text: Give up on funding and go back to the regular offers
choices.label: BACK_TO_OFFERS

ST_REF_CHASE.title: The analog professor.
ST_REF_CHASE.speaker: Your old department, {city}
ST_REF_CHASE.dialogue: Your referee forgot his portal password and won't use 'these online things'. The application portal closes in 48 hours.

choices.text: Buy a carton of malt, brave the traffic and sit him down at a PC yourself
choices.label: MALT_DIPLOMACY
choices.feedback: He types with one finger and calls you 'my best student'. Submitted with 3 hours left.

choices.text: Write the letter yourself and ask him to just upload it
choices.label: SELF_WRITTEN_REF

choices.text: Ask your project supervisor, who actually answers email, instead
choices.label: SECOND_REFEREE

success.feedback: She uploads a strong letter the same evening.
success.label: SUPERVISOR_UPLOADED

fail.feedback: She's at a conference. The portal closes. Back to regular offers.
fail.label: PORTAL_CLOSED

ST_REF_FAKE.title: The letter in your own words.
ST_REF_FAKE.speaker: University admissions office
ST_REF_FAKE.dialogue: The admissions officer notices the reference reads exactly like your statement of purpose, comma for comma. They call your referee.

outcome.title: Self-written reference
outcome.subtitle: The offer is withdrawn.
outcome.lesson: A reference must be the referee's own words. Writing your own and submitting it as theirs is academic fraud: offers are withdrawn, and a fraudulent document in a visa file is misrepresentation.

ST_FUNDED.title: Fully funded.
ST_FUNDED.speaker: Your inbox
ST_FUNDED.dialogue: Offer of admission: research master's, tuition covered, CAD 26,000 a year from a research assistantship. You read it eleven times.

choices.text: Accept, and build the rest of your funds file
choices.label: ACCEPTED_FUNDING
choices.feedback: Funding counts in your proof of funds. Most Canadian programs don't need the GRE; your supervisor's yes matters more.

FY_LANDLORD.title: Mr. Henderson's basement.
FY_LANDLORD.speaker: Mr. Henderson (Landlord)
FY_LANDLORD.dialogue: The furnace clanks. Mr. Henderson flips your papers. 'I ran your name through Equifax: no Canadian credit. No Canadian job reference either. How do I know you'll pay on the first of every month?'

choices.text: 'I just landed last week! How can I have Canadian credit? Look at my bank statement!'
choices.label: DEFENSIVE

success.feedback: He shrugs. 'Fine, fair point.'
success.label: HE_SHRUGGED

fail.feedback: His face closes. 'I'll let you know.' He won't.
fail.label: REJECTED

choices.text: 'I understand. While my credit builds, I can pay the last month's deposit now and show my savings.'
choices.label: PREPAY_OFFER
choices.feedback: In Ontario a landlord can't demand more than a last-month deposit, but showing savings reassures them. Don't hand over extra months under pressure.

choices.text: '{relName} in {relCity} will co-sign as guarantor, with an employment letter and strong credit.'
choices.label: GUARANTOR_RELATIVE
choices.feedback: Your network's credit history stands in for yours. That's what guarantors are for.

FY_LANDLORD_2.title: 'This is a quiet house.'
FY_LANDLORD_2.speaker: Mr. Henderson (Landlord)
FY_LANDLORD_2.dialogue: 'My family lives upstairs. Am I going to hear loud parties, or people coming in and out?'

choices.text: 'I work full-time and study for my licence at night. I'll mostly be here to sleep.'
choices.label: QUIET_TENANT
choices.feedback: Exactly what a landlord wants to hear. Lease signed.

choices.text: 'Friends from the {faithHub} might come by sometimes, but we're good people.'
choices.label: SOCIAL_TENANT

success.feedback: 'That's fine, just keep it down after ten.' Lease signed.
success.label: SIGNED

fail.feedback: He 'has another applicant'. Back to the listings for a week.
fail.label: OTHER_APPLICANT

choices.text: 'Could we put the house rules in the lease so we're both clear?'
choices.label: RULES_IN_LEASE
choices.feedback: He likes that. The Ontario standard lease has room for exactly this.

TT_START.title: Ten years, no payslip.
TT_START.speaker: Electrical market, {city}
TT_START.dialogue: You can wire a duplex blindfolded. Canada's trades draws want electricians, plumbers, carpenters and welders. But every naira you ever earned came in cash, and immigration counts what it can verify.

choices.text: Electrician: you've done estates, solar and industrial wiring
choices.label: ELECTRICIAN

choices.text: Plumber: boreholes, pumps, and every leaking soak-away in {area}
choices.label: PLUMBER

choices.text: Welder and fabricator: gates, frames and a few tanker repairs
choices.label: WELDER

TT_PAPERWORK.title: Proof of the hands.
TT_PAPERWORK.speaker: Your oga's workshop, {area}
TT_PAPERWORK.dialogue: You need letters on letterhead: dates, hours, duties, pay. Your oga writes nothing down, and his 'company' is a kiosk.

choices.text: Ask oga for a reference letter, and register your own business with CAC so new jobs have invoices
choices.label: REAL_RECORDS
choices.feedback: Slow and boring. Every invoice from now on is evidence.

choices.text: Join a registered contractor with payslips and tax deductions, for less money
choices.label: PAYSLIP_JOB
choices.feedback: Smaller pay, real payslips. Officers love payslips.

choices.text: Buy a 'ten years experience' letter from a man in a cyber cafe
choices.label: FAKE_LETTER

TT_MORE_YEARS.title: Keep building the file.
TT_MORE_YEARS.speaker: Construction site, {city}
TT_MORE_YEARS.dialogue: One documented year isn't enough: Federal Skilled Trades wants two years of full-time experience in the last five.

choices.text: Another year of documented work, every receipt filed
choices.label: SECOND_YEAR
choices.feedback: Two documented years. The file finally looks like your life.

choices.text: Count your old cash jobs too; you'll explain them if asked
choices.label: CASH_YEARS

success.feedback: Two old clients sign sworn statements with their phone numbers. It might be enough.
success.label: SWORN

fail.feedback: Nobody can confirm those years. Only your documented year counts.
fail.label: UNVERIFIABLE

TT_LANGUAGE.title: The lower bar.
TT_LANGUAGE.speaker: Test centre, {city}
TT_LANGUAGE.dialogue: Good news: the trades program asks for CLB 5 in speaking and listening, and CLB 4 in reading and writing. Higher scores still add points.

choices.text: Prepare for a month, then write CELPIP or IELTS General
choices.label: PREPARED

success.feedback: CLB 7. Above the bar, and more points.
success.label: CLB7

fail.feedback: CLB 5. Just enough.
fail.label: CLB5

choices.text: Write it next week; how hard can it be?
choices.label: WINGED_IT

success.feedback: CLB 5. You scraped through.
success.label: SCRAPED

fail.feedback: Reading came in at CLB 3. Below the bar; you'll have to rebook.
fail.label: BELOW_BAR

TT_CERT.title: Certificate or job offer.
TT_CERT.speaker: Video call with Alberta
TT_CERT.dialogue: The program also needs either a Canadian job offer or a certificate of qualification from a province, which means an assessment of your experience and a trade exam.

choices.text: Apply for a provincial trade assessment and book the exam
choices.label: TRADE_EXAM

success.feedback: Passed. A provincial certificate of qualification with your name on it.
success.label: CERTIFIED

fail.feedback: Failed the code section by four marks. You can rewrite in 90 days.
fail.label: FAILED_EXAM

choices.text: Cold-message 40 contractors on LinkedIn with photos of your work
choices.label: LINKEDIN

success.feedback: A Calgary contractor offers a one-year job, subject to your PR. A real offer.
success.label: OFFER

fail.feedback: Two 'interested', zero offers.
fail.label: GHOSTED

choices.text: Pay an agent ₦900k for a 'Red Seal certificate, no exam'
choices.label: RED_SEAL_SCAM

TT_ITA.title: Trades draw.
TT_ITA.speaker: IRCC portal
TT_ITA.dialogue: 'Invitation to apply.' The trades draw cutoff sat far below the general rounds. Four months later, you land in Edmonton in January.

choices.text: Report to the site on Monday
choices.label: LANDED

TT_WINTER.title: −27°C on the scaffold.
TT_WINTER.speaker: Construction site, Edmonton
TT_WINTER.dialogue: Your first outdoor shift. Your fingers stop working after twenty minutes. The foreman says 'You'll get used to it' and doesn't look convinced.

choices.text: Spend your first paycheque on proper winter work gear
choices.label: GEAR
choices.feedback: Insulated boots, liners, a balaclava. You stop counting your toes.

choices.text: Tough it out in your Lagos jacket
choices.label: TOUGH_IT

success.feedback: You survive the week and buy gear on Friday.
success.label: SURVIVED

fail.feedback: Frostnip on two fingers. Three days off, unpaid.
fail.label: FROSTNIP

TT_WIN.title: Journeyperson.
TT_WIN.speaker: Edmonton
TT_WIN.dialogue: Your Alberta ticket, your union card, and an apprentice who calls you 'boss'. Red Seal is the next exam.

outcome.title: Permanent resident, working your trade
outcome.subtitle: Your hands, finally on paper.
outcome.lesson: Federal Skilled Trades and trades category draws reward documented, full-time trade experience. Most trades are regulated by provinces: you work under a provincial certificate, and Red Seal lets you work across Canada.

TT_NOT_YET.title: Not yet.
TT_NOT_YET.speaker: IRCC portal
TT_NOT_YET.dialogue: Your profile is missing something: two documented years, CLB 5, or a certificate or job offer.

outcome.title: Not eligible yet
outcome.subtitle: The trade is real. The paperwork isn't there yet.
outcome.lesson: Federal Skilled Trades needs all three: two years of full-time trade experience in the last five, the language minimums, and a Canadian job offer or a provincial certificate of qualification.

TT_FAKE_LETTER.title: The company didn't exist.
TT_FAKE_LETTER.speaker: IRCC portal
TT_FAKE_LETTER.dialogue: IRCC phoned the number on your letter. It belongs to a cyber cafe.

outcome.title: Fake experience letter
outcome.subtitle: Refused, with a five-year ban.
outcome.lesson: Fake experience letters are misrepresentation: refusal and a five-year ban. Officers verify employers by phone, address and tax records.

TT_RED_SEAL_SCAM.title: Gold foil.
TT_RED_SEAL_SCAM.speaker: Agent's office, {city}
TT_RED_SEAL_SCAM.dialogue: The 'Red Seal' certificate has gold foil and a spelling mistake. Red Seal is an exam you write in Canada, not a document you buy.

outcome.title: Bought a 'Red Seal'
outcome.subtitle: ₦900k, no exam, no value.
outcome.lesson: Red Seal endorsements come from passing the interprovincial exam after you qualify in a province. Nobody sells one.

TT_BURNOUT.title: Burnt out.
TT_BURNOUT.speaker: {area}, {city}
TT_BURNOUT.dialogue: Two jobs, one generator, no rest. Your body made the decision for you.

outcome.title: Burnt out
outcome.subtitle: Rest, then rebuild the file.
outcome.lesson: Pace the grind: the file takes years, and it waits for you.

PN_START.title: Toronto is full.
PN_START.speaker: {area}, {city}
PN_START.dialogue: Your CRS is {crs}. General draws need 500+. A provincial nomination adds 600 points. The catch: provinces nominate people who will actually live there.

choices.text: Saskatchewan: in-demand jobs list and lower rent
choices.label: SASKATCHEWAN

choices.text: Manitoba: they favour people with a real connection to the province
choices.label: MANITOBA

choices.text: Nova Scotia: healthcare and trades priorities, and the ocean
choices.label: NOVA_SCOTIA

choices.text: A Rural Community Immigration Pilot town: Thunder Bay, Sudbury, Brandon, North Okanagan Shuswap and others
choices.label: RCIP

PN_RESEARCH.title: Read the stream.
PN_RESEARCH.speaker: Provincial website
PN_RESEARCH.dialogue: Every province runs its own streams, and they change. Some are linked to Express Entry (+600 CRS); others are separate paper applications.

choices.text: Read the stream rules properly and match your job to their in-demand list
choices.label: READ_RULES
choices.feedback: Boring and decisive. Half the group chat applies to streams they don't qualify for.

choices.text: Ask {relName} in {relCity} what they know
choices.label: ASK_RELATIVE
choices.feedback: A relative living in the province can count as a connection for some streams.

PN_TIES.title: Build real ties.
PN_TIES.location: Video calls, job boards, the Naija association
PN_TIES.speaker: Video calls, job boards, the Naija association
PN_TIES.dialogue: Provinces want proof you'll stay: a job offer, past study or work there, family, or an exploratory visit.

choices.text: Apply to employers in smaller towns, not just the big cities
choices.label: SMALL_TOWNS
choices.feedback: Moose Jaw, Brandon, Truro. Less competition, more replies.

choices.text: Book an exploratory visit on a visitor visa: meet employers and the community
choices.label: EXPLORATORY
choices.feedback: Some streams count an exploratory visit. You interview in person and walk the town in −20°C.

choices.text: Join the province's Nigerian association online and volunteer remotely
choices.label: ASSOCIATION

PN_OFFER.title: The rural employer.
PN_OFFER.speaker: Video call, Moose Jaw
PN_OFFER.dialogue: A trucking firm's HR manager likes you. 'We need people who'll stay. Most newcomers leave for Toronto in a year.'

choices.text: 'I'm here to stay. My budget, my {faithHub}, my kids' school: I've looked them up.'
choices.label: STAY_PLAN

success.feedback: A one-year offer, conditional on your nomination.
success.label: OFFER

fail.feedback: 'We'll keep your file.' No offer, but the call counts as a contact.
fail.label: NO_OFFER

choices.text: 'Honestly, I'd move to Toronto eventually.'
choices.label: HONEST_TORONTO
choices.feedback: Honest. It also tells them you're the person they just described.

PN_NOMINATED.speaker: IRCC portal
PN_NOMINATED.dialogue: Provincial nomination. Your Express Entry profile jumps by 600 points. The next draw invites you within weeks.

choices.text: Accept the nomination
choices.label: ACCEPTED
choices.feedback: +600 CRS. An invitation is almost guaranteed.

PN_INTENT.title: 'Come to Toronto, bro.'
PN_INTENT.speaker: WhatsApp, after landing
PN_INTENT.dialogue: You're a PR now. Your cousin in Brampton: 'Why you dey that cold village? Come Toronto, jobs dey here.'

choices.text: Settle in the province, as you told them, and build there
choices.label: SETTLED
choices.feedback: You meant it. Your rent is half of Brampton's.

choices.text: Move to Toronto in month one; you only said the province to get the points
choices.label: INTENT_LIE

PN_SETTLED.title: Prairie resident.
PN_SETTLED.speaker: Saskatoon
PN_SETTLED.dialogue: A two-bedroom for the price of a Brampton basement. The Naija association brings jollof to your housewarming.

outcome.title: Nominated, landed, settled
outcome.subtitle: The +600 was the easy part.
outcome.lesson: Provincial nominees are expected to intend to live in the province. Permanent residents have mobility rights, but saying you'd settle when you never meant to can be treated as misrepresentation.

PN_INTENT_LIE.title: Toronto in disguise.
PN_INTENT_LIE.speaker: Brampton
PN_INTENT_LIE.dialogue: A year later your citizenship file asks where you've lived. The province flagged you: you never even took the job they nominated you for.

outcome.title: Misrepresented your intent
outcome.subtitle: The province remembers.
outcome.lesson: Permanent residents can live anywhere in Canada, but your intent when you applied matters. Telling a province you'd settle while planning to leave can be treated as misrepresentation, with serious consequences for your status.

PN_NOT_SELECTED.title: Not selected.
PN_NOT_SELECTED.speaker: Provincial portal
PN_NOT_SELECTED.dialogue: No nomination this intake. Your ties to the province were too thin.

outcome.title: Not selected
outcome.subtitle: Build real ties and try again.
outcome.lesson: Provinces nominate people likely to stay: a job offer, past study or work there, family, or an exploratory visit all help.

PN_BURNOUT.title: Burnt out.
PN_BURNOUT.speaker: {area}, {city}
PN_BURNOUT.dialogue: Too many portals, not enough sleep.

outcome.title: Burnt out
outcome.subtitle: Rest first.
outcome.lesson: Streams reopen. Your health doesn't.

SF_START.title: Who flies first?
SF_START.speaker: Your parlour, {area}
SF_START.dialogue: Your admission is for a 16-month master's, so your spouse can apply for an open work permit later. Today you decide: who goes now, and where do the kids stay?

choices.text: You go alone. The kids stay with your spouse, who keeps the job and the naira income
choices.label: SOLO_VANGUARD
choices.feedback: The 'pilot-passenger' plan: your spouse funds the transition from home.

choices.text: You take the kids. Your spouse stays to work and follows later
choices.label: SINGLE_PARENT_PILOT
choices.feedback: In many provinces, children of study-permit holders can attend public school; check the school board.

SF_AIRPORT.title: Departures, {airportCode}.
SF_AIRPORT.speaker: Departure hall, {airportCode}
SF_AIRPORT.dialogue: Four Ghana Must Go bags, a carry-on of foodstuff, and a goodbye in the car park that nobody rehearsed.

choices.text: Pay for the overweight bags; everything comes
choices.label: PAID_OVERWEIGHT
choices.feedback: Expensive, but your spouse packed every bag with love and pepper.

choices.text: Repack on the floor and leave the stockfish behind
choices.label: REPACKED
choices.feedback: Saved CAD 350. The stockfish will be missed.

SF_REMIT.title: Two currencies.
SF_REMIT.speaker: Your basement room, Winnipeg
SF_REMIT.dialogue: Rent is due here in four days. At home, school fees are due in two weeks. Your Canada wallet and your home wallet both look worried.

choices.text: Send CAD 400 home now
choices.label: SENT_HOME
choices.feedback: The rate eats a little. Your spouse sends a voice note: 'Thank you, darling.'

choices.text: Take an extra 6 hours of delivery shifts, within your 24-hour limit, then send it
choices.label: EXTRA_SHIFTS
choices.feedback: Study permits allow up to 24 hours a week off-campus during classes.

choices.text: Ask your spouse to cover it from home this month
choices.label: HOME_COVERS
choices.feedback: It's covered. The tone of the next call isn't.

SF_CALLS.title: Time zones.
SF_CALLS.speaker: Video call, 6 a.m. your time
SF_CALLS.dialogue: Lagos is five hours ahead. Your calls keep landing when one of you is asleep. Last week your spouse asked who you were 'always out with'. The answer is the library and the warehouse, but distance doesn't hear answers.

choices.text: Fix a call time every day, and share your shift schedule
choices.label: FIXED_CALLS
choices.feedback: Boring, predictable, and it works. Trust needs routine.

choices.text: Send a surprise: data bundle, flowers and the kids' favourite snacks
choices.label: SURPRISE
choices.feedback: It lands on a bad day and makes it a good one.

choices.text: You're too tired to explain; you'll talk on the weekend
choices.label: TOO_TIRED
choices.feedback: You slept. The silence filled itself in.

SF_KIDS.title: 'When is Daddy coming?'
SF_KIDS.speaker: Your basement room, Winnipeg
SF_KIDS.dialogue: Your youngest won't sleep. She asks the same question every night and draws Lagos with crayons.

choices.text: Book a weekly video storytime with your spouse
choices.label: STORYTIME
choices.feedback: Bedtime stories from Lagos, every Sunday. She sleeps.

choices.text: Find a newcomer family program at the library
choices.label: LIBRARY_PROGRAM
choices.feedback: Free, warm, and full of kids who also miss someone.

choices.text: Keep busy; she'll adjust
choices.label: SHE_WILL_ADJUST
choices.feedback: Children adjust. They also remember.

SF_HOME_CRISIS.title: The generator died.
SF_HOME_CRISIS.speaker: WhatsApp from Lagos
SF_HOME_CRISIS.dialogue: Your spouse: 'Gen don die. Mechanic says ₦280k. Kids have exams this week.' Your shift starts in an hour.

choices.text: Send CAD 260 for the repair
choices.label: FIXED_GEN

choices.text: Tell them to use the home wallet; you're stretched
choices.label: HOME_WALLET
choices.feedback: Fair, and it still feels like you weren't there.

SF_SOWP.title: The open work permit.
SF_SOWP.speaker: IRCC portal
SF_SOWP.dialogue: Your spouse applies for an open work permit, based on your 16-month master's. Now everything you've held together gets tested.

choices.text: Help prepare it properly: your enrolment letter, marriage certificate, photos, funds
choices.label: PROPER_SOWP
choices.feedback: A clean application. The wait is still the wait.

choices.text: Leave it to an unlicensed 'agent' to save time
choices.label: AGENT_SOWP
choices.feedback: He uploads the wrong certificate. A request for documents adds months.

choices.text: Quit the program and fly home to the family
choices.label: WENT_HOME

SF_REUNITED.title: Arrivals, Pearson.
SF_REUNITED.speaker: Toronto Pearson, Terminal 3
SF_REUNITED.dialogue: Your spouse walks out with a work permit and two bags of foodstuff. The kids scream. Strangers clap.

outcome.title: Reunited
outcome.subtitle: Two wallets, two time zones, one family again.
outcome.lesson: A spouse's open work permit depends on the student's program (16+ month master's, doctorate, or certain professional programs since 2025). Split families that budget for both homes and talk every day are the ones that make it to arrivals.

SF_WENT_HOME.title: Flew home.
SF_WENT_HOME.speaker: {airportCode}
SF_WENT_HOME.dialogue: You chose the family over the program. Nobody at home calls it failure.

outcome.title: Went home to the family
outcome.subtitle: The program can wait. Some things can't.
outcome.lesson: Leaving your program ends your study permit's purpose. You can apply again later, and a clean history helps.

SF_BREAKDOWN.title: The strain won.
SF_BREAKDOWN.speaker: Video call, 3 a.m.
SF_BREAKDOWN.dialogue: The call ends without goodbye. Distance found every crack the money and the hours had covered.

outcome.title: The strain won
outcome.subtitle: Distance found every crack.
outcome.lesson: Split-family moves are some of the hardest. Plan both budgets, a daily call routine and the work-permit timeline before anyone flies.

LAGOS_LOOKALIKE.title: 'The owner no need am again.'
LAGOS_LOOKALIKE.location: Behind a shop near the passport office, {city}
LAGOS_LOOKALIKE.speaker: Behind a shop near the passport office, {city}
LAGOS_LOOKALIKE.dialogue: He opens a green booklet. A real Nigerian passport, a real Canadian visa, a stranger's name and a stranger's face that looks a bit like yours. 'The owner no need am again,' he says, and doesn't say why. ₦3.5 million. 'Or I fit do you fresh one, your own picture, another person details.'

choices.text: Walk away. Report him at the immigration desk inside, then book the real appointment: CAD 185 in visa and biometrics fees
Walk away. You can't afford the real fees yet, so it's the weekend hustle first
Pay for the lookalike passport. Same face, small difference
choices.label: BOUGHT_PASSPORT

choices.text: Ask for the 'fresh one': your photo, someone else's details
choices.label: FAKE_PASSPORT

LAGOS_LOOKALIKE_FAIL.title: Someone else's name
LAGOS_LOOKALIKE_FAIL.speaker: Departure gate
LAGOS_LOOKALIKE_FAIL.dialogue: At the gate, the officer asks your date of birth. You say the one you memorised, a second too slowly. She looks at the photo, then at you, then calls a colleague. The passport was reported stolen months ago. Its real owner has been fighting to get a new one.

outcome.title: Impostor at the gate
outcome.subtitle: Arrested before boarding. The ₦3.5m is gone.
outcome.lesson: Travelling on another person's passport is impostor fraud. It's a crime in Nigeria, and in Canada using a false or someone else's document is misrepresentation (a five-year ban) and can be prosecuted. Canada takes fingerprints with most visas and can check them on arrival. 'Lookalike' passports are often stolen from real people.

LAGOS_FAKE_PASSPORT_FAIL.title: A passport that doesn't exist
LAGOS_FAKE_PASSPORT_FAIL.speaker: Visa application centre
LAGOS_FAKE_PASSPORT_FAIL.dialogue: The 'fresh' passport looks perfect to you. The visa application asks for its number. The number belongs to nobody, or to somebody else. Your application is flagged, and your real name, face and fingerprints are now on file next to a forged document.

outcome.title: Forged passport
outcome.subtitle: Refused, banned, and your money's gone.
outcome.lesson: A forged passport is document fraud in Nigeria and in Canada. IRCC refuses the application for misrepresentation and bars you for five years, and the record follows your real fingerprints into every future application. The only real passport comes from the Nigeria Immigration Service, at the official fee.

EE_WEEK.title: 4:00 a.m. Again.
EE_WEEK.speaker: {area}, {city}
EE_WEEK.dialogue: Alarm at 4:00. Out by 4:40, or {city} traffic eats your morning. At your desk by 7:30, home after 9 p.m. if the road is kind. The IELTS book on your table still has the receipt inside it. When exactly are you supposed to read?

choices.text: Study on the {bus}: listening practice in your earphones, one reading test a day
choices.label: BUS_STUDY
choices.feedback: Two hours a day in traffic, finally working for you. The conductor now knows the word 'nevertheless'.

choices.text: Wake at 3 a.m. and study before the traffic starts
choices.label: THREE_AM
choices.feedback: The quietest hour in {city}. Also the sleepiest. Your colleagues ask why your eyes are red.

choices.text: Pay for weekend classes at a prep centre
choices.label: PREP_CLASS
choices.feedback: A tutor who has seen a thousand writing tasks. Worth it, if you actually go.

choices.text: Too tired. You'll read when work calms down
choices.label: LATER
choices.feedback: Work does not calm down. Work has never calmed down.

EE_WEEKEND.title: Saturday has three invitations.
EE_WEEKEND.speaker: {area}, {city}
EE_WEEKEND.dialogue: Your cousin's wedding, a colleague's child naming and your neighbour's father's burial, all on Saturday. The {partyCloth} for the wedding is ₦35,000. Your laundry has been waiting since last Saturday.

choices.text: Skip the owambe. Send your gift by transfer and study all Saturday
choices.label: SKIP_OWAMBE
choices.feedback: Aunty calls: 'Shebi you don japa already? We no see your face.' You did a full mock test, though.

choices.text: Show face at the wedding for one hour, then home to study
choices.label: SHOW_FACE
choices.feedback: You said one hour. It was four. The jollof was worth it; the reading test was not done.

choices.text: Wedding, naming, burial and laundry: do it all
choices.label: DO_IT_ALL
choices.feedback: Everybody saw you. Nobody saw you study.

EE_SUNDAY.title: The one day {city} lets you breathe.
EE_SUNDAY.speaker: {area}, {city}
EE_SUNDAY.dialogue: {FaithHub} matters to you, and so does this test. The {faithGroup} is expecting you. The exam is in six weeks.

choices.text: Tell the {faithGroup} you're on leave for two months. First service, then home to study
choices.label: FIRST_SERVICE
choices.feedback: The choir master is not happy, but the pastor says 'go and prosper'. You do a writing task before dinner.

choices.text: Stay for the whole programme: service, thanksgiving, meeting. Four and a half hours
choices.label: FULL_PROGRAMME
choices.feedback: Your spirit is full and your notebook is empty.

choices.text: Jumu'ah was on Friday at lunchtime. Sunday is yours: a full mock test, 9 a.m. to 1 p.m.
choices.label: SUNDAY_MOCK
choices.feedback: Listening, reading, writing, and the speaking part into your phone's recorder. You sound better than you thought.

choices.text: Sleep. Your body has filed a formal complaint
choices.label: SLEEP
choices.feedback: Twelve hours. You wake up a new person who still hasn't studied.

EE_WES_VERIFY.title: WES has emailed your school.
EE_WES_VERIFY.speaker: University registry
EE_WES_VERIFY.dialogue: You opened your WES account first, because the registry won't send anything without your WES reference number. The transcript finally reached WES. Now WES wants the school to confirm it's genuine, the registry's official email last replied in March, and WES won't start until its fee is paid. A clerk leans over: 'Drop something for the boys and it will move.'

choices.text: Pay the WES fee by card, print WES's request, and follow up at the registry every week, politely
choices.label: FOLLOW_UP
choices.feedback: Week five, the registrar signs it off. WES says 'verified'. Tip: WES gives your reference number when you submit the application; you can pay after, but nothing is evaluated until the money lands.

choices.text: Ask whether your school can confirm by its official email, which some Nigerian schools now do
choices.label: OFFICIAL_EMAIL

success.feedback: Your school is set up for it. The registry emails WES from its official address and you're verified in nine days.

fail.feedback: Not your school, not yet. Back to the registry queue for four more weeks.

choices.text: 'Drop something for the boys': ₦50k to the clerk
choices.label: BRIBE
choices.feedback: He replies to WES from his personal Gmail. WES only accepts confirmation from the institution itself, so it bounces. The ₦50k is gone, the bribe was a crime, and you're back at the registry.

EE_SECRET.title: Who told HR?
EE_SECRET.speaker: Your office, {city}
EE_SECRET.dialogue: Somebody saw the IELTS book in your bag. By Friday the office WhatsApp is guessing. In this company, people who 'want to japa' stop getting promotions, or get let go first. And Express Entry will need a reference letter from this same company.

choices.text: Say nothing. Work hard, and ask HR for the reference letter after your invitation
choices.label: QUIET
choices.feedback: Quiet is normal. Reference letters are routine HR work; you'll ask when you need it, with your current duties on it.

choices.text: Tell your manager you plan to leave in a year, and offer to train your replacement
choices.label: TOLD_MANAGER

success.feedback: He japa'd to Leeds and came back. 'I go write you the letter. Just train the new boy well.'

fail.feedback: By Monday you're off the big project, and your bonus quietly shrinks. Nobody says why.

choices.text: Post 'Canada, here I come 🇨🇦' on your status
choices.label: POSTED
choices.feedback: HR calls you in: 'We are restructuring.' You keep the job, lose the promotion, and your colleague takes your seat by the AC.

NURSE_NCLEX.title: Authorised to write. Not in Nigeria.
NURSE_NCLEX.speaker: Your nursing college email
NURSE_NCLEX.dialogue: Your NNAS report is done (BC no longer requires one), and the provincial college has decided you can write the NCLEX-RN. There's no NCLEX centre in Nigeria. The closest are Nairobi and Johannesburg.

choices.text: Nairobi: a short online entry step for Nigerians, a flight and three nights
choices.label: NAIROBI
choices.feedback: Many Nigerian nurses pick Nairobi because getting into Kenya is simpler than getting a South African visa.

success.feedback: Pass. The exam shut off early and you didn't know whether that was good until the email came.
success.label: NCLEX_PASS

fail.feedback: Not this time. The college lets you rebook after the waiting period.
fail.label: NCLEX_RETAKE

choices.text: Johannesburg: apply for a South African visa first, and hope it comes before your test window closes
choices.label: JOBURG

success.feedback: The visa lands with a week to spare. Pass.
success.label: NCLEX_PASS

fail.feedback: The visa comes two days after your window closed. Rebook, repay.
fail.label: VISA_LATE

choices.text: Write it after you land in Canada
choices.label: IN_CANADA
choices.feedback: You can sit it in Canada too, but until you pass you can't work as an RN there. Many work as care aides in the meantime.

FY_OLD_JOB.title: Your Lagos job is still open on your laptop.
FY_OLD_JOB.speaker: A rented room, first week
FY_OLD_JOB.dialogue: You landed, but you never resigned. Plenty of people don't, straight away: Canadian jobs take months, and a salary from home buys time. Managers sometimes negotiate remote months; people close to retirement wait it out. Lagos is five or six hours ahead.

choices.text: Ask your boss honestly for three remote months while you hand over
choices.label: REMOTE_ASKED

success.feedback: He agrees. Your 9 a.m. stand-up is at 3 a.m. here, but the naira salary covers rent. Declare it on your Canadian tax return.

fail.feedback: He says no, kindly. You resign by email and train your replacement on Zoom for a week.

choices.text: Resign properly: notice, handover, goodbye cake
choices.label: RESIGNED
choices.feedback: Clean exit. Your old boss becomes your best reference.

choices.text: Keep the job and don't tell them you've left Nigeria
choices.label: HIDDEN_REMOTE
choices.feedback: Camera off, a generator sound playing from YouTube. They find out at the next all-hands. You're fired, and the reference you'll need is gone.

AIP_START.title: Four provinces by the sea.
AIP_START.speaker: {area}, {city}
AIP_START.dialogue: {RelName} forwards a link: 'Atlantic Canada is hiring from abroad.' The Atlantic Immigration Program covers Nova Scotia, New Brunswick, Prince Edward Island, and Newfoundland and Labrador. The catch: only employers the province has designated can hire you through it, each province has a yearly limit, and you need about a year (1,560 hours) of paid work in the last five years.

choices.text: Nova Scotia: Halifax hospitals, trucking and tech
choices.label: NOVA_SCOTIA

choices.text: New Brunswick: Moncton, bilingual and cheaper rent
choices.label: NEW_BRUNSWICK
choices.feedback: Heads up: New Brunswick paused AIP once its 2025 allocation ran out, and paused new employer designations in early 2026.

choices.text: Newfoundland and Labrador: St. John's, healthcare and the windiest city you'll ever love
choices.label: NEWFOUNDLAND

choices.text: Prince Edward Island: small, friendly, and a few jobs at a time
choices.label: PEI

AIP_JOBHUNT.title: Designated employers only.
AIP_JOBHUNT.speaker: Job boards, {area}
AIP_JOBHUNT.dialogue: The province publishes its list of designated employers. Job boards are full of Atlantic ads, but most of those employers aren't designated. A WhatsApp 'recruiter' says he has an AIP job in Halifax: CAD 3,000 'processing'.

choices.text: Apply directly to designated employers in your field, from the province's own list, with a Canadian-style CV
choices.label: DESIGNATED

choices.text: Apply to every Atlantic job ad you see: 200 applications
choices.label: SPRAY
choices.feedback: Most weren't designated. An offer from them can't be used for AIP.

choices.text: Pay the 'recruiter' CAD 3,000 for the AIP job
choices.label: PAID_FOR_JOB

AIP_INTERVIEW.title: 10 a.m. in Halifax. 2 p.m. at your desk.
AIP_INTERVIEW.speaker: Video call
