AIP_INTERVIEW.dialogue: A designated employer wants a video interview. Atlantic Canada is four or five hours behind {city}, so it lands in the middle of your workday, and your Oga has a meeting at 2.

choices.text: Ask to move it to 7 a.m. their time and take it from your car at lunch
choices.label: LUNCH_CALL

success.feedback: They move it. You answer about {interviewHook} with a sunshade on the windscreen. They like you.

fail.feedback: The car park is loud and the network drops twice. 'We'll be in touch.'

choices.text: Take the day off officially for 'personal matters' and prepare properly
choices.label: DAY_OFF

success.feedback: Quiet room, good light, notes on the wall. You tell the {interviewHook} well. Offer pending.

fail.feedback: Good interview. They chose someone already in Halifax.

choices.text: Do it at your desk with one earphone in
choices.label: AT_DESK

success.feedback: Nobody noticed. Somehow. They liked your answers.

fail.feedback: Oga walks in mid-answer. You say 'yes sir' to both of them.

AIP_SECOND.title: Another designated employer replies.
AIP_SECOND.speaker: Email
AIP_SECOND.dialogue: No offer from the first one. A second designated employer, smaller, in a town you had to find on the map, wants to talk.

choices.text: Research the town, the employer and the bus routes, then interview
choices.label: RESEARCHED

success.feedback: 'You've looked us up. Nobody does that.' Offer.

fail.feedback: They went with an internal candidate.

choices.text: Interview as you are; no time to research
choices.label: AS_IS

success.feedback: They liked you anyway. Offer.

fail.feedback: 'We'll keep your CV on file.'

AIP_OFFER.title: The offer, and the fine print.
AIP_OFFER.speaker: Email
AIP_OFFER.dialogue: Full-time, at least 30 hours a week, not seasonal, and at least a year after you become a permanent resident. HR writes: 'We'll refer you to a settlement provider and request your endorsement.' Then a second email arrives from a 'partner agency': 'Pay the CAD 230 employer compliance fee and your endorsement fee to this account.'

choices.text: Accept the offer. Reply that the employer pays the compliance fee, and check with HR on their official email
choices.label: VERIFIED
choices.feedback: Right: the employer pays the compliance fee through IRCC's Employer Portal. HR has never heard of the 'partner agency'.

choices.text: Pay the 'partner agency' to be safe
choices.label: PAID_FEE

AIP_LANGUAGE.title: CLB 5. Not CLB 9.
AIP_LANGUAGE.speaker: Test centre, {city}
AIP_LANGUAGE.dialogue: Your job is TEER 0 to 3, so AIP needs CLB 5 in all four skills (CLB 4 for TEER 4 jobs). No points, no ranking: you clear the bar or you don't. Any IRCC-approved test counts: IELTS General, CELPIP or PTE Core. Pick the one you're most comfortable with.

choices.text: CELPIP-General in Lagos or Ibadan: computer-based, Canadian accents
choices.label: CELPIP

success.feedback: CELPIP 8 across the board: CLB 8. Far above the bar.

fail.feedback: CELPIP 5 in writing: CLB 5. Just enough.

choices.text: IELTS General, because that's what everyone writes
choices.label: IELTS

success.feedback: IELTS 6.5 overall: CLB 7 or better in every skill.

fail.feedback: Writing 5.0: CLB 5. Just over the bar.

choices.text: No time to prepare: book the earliest date and wing it
choices.label: WING_IT

success.feedback: CLB 5. You cleared it by the skin of your teeth.

fail.feedback: CLB 4 in writing: below the CLB 5 your job needs.

AIP_RETAKE.title: One band short.
AIP_RETAKE.speaker: Test centre, {city}
AIP_RETAKE.dialogue: CLB 4 won't do for a TEER 0 to 3 job. Your employer says they'll wait a few weeks.

choices.text: Rebook, and actually prepare this time
choices.label: RETAKE
choices.feedback: CLB 6. Over the bar.

AIP_ECA.title: Your certificate, assessed.
AIP_ECA.speaker: University registry
AIP_ECA.dialogue: AIP needs at least a Canadian high-school equivalent, so your Nigerian education needs an ECA. Same saga: WES reference number, transcripts sent by the school, verification.

choices.text: Do it properly: reference number first, then chase the registry
choices.label: PROPER_ECA

choices.text: A 'connect' can print the transcripts tonight
choices.label: FAKE_TRANSCRIPT

AIP_SETTLE.title: The settlement plan.
AIP_SETTLE.location: Video call with a settlement counsellor
AIP_SETTLE.speaker: Video call with a settlement counsellor
AIP_SETTLE.dialogue: Your employer refers you to a designated settlement provider: ISANS in Nova Scotia, the Association for New Canadians in Newfoundland and Labrador, or a local agency in New Brunswick or PEI. A counsellor video-calls you for a needs assessment: family, housing, budget, health, and what worries you. The plan you sign goes with your endorsement.

choices.text: Be honest: your budget, the family you send money to, your fear of winter
choices.label: HONEST_PLAN
choices.feedback: A plan for your real life: a room on a bus route, a winter-clothes list, the date of newcomer orientation.

choices.text: Say everything is fine and you need nothing
choices.label: THIN_PLAN
choices.feedback: The plan is thin. When you land, nobody knows you need help with housing.

AIP_ENDORSED.title: Endorsement certificate.
AIP_ENDORSED.speaker: Provincial email
AIP_ENDORSED.dialogue: The province endorses your job offer and, because your employer asked, sends a referral letter for a work permit. Your employer submits the offer in IRCC's Employer Portal, pays the compliance fee and sends you the offer of employment number. You can apply for permanent residence, and for a two-year work permit tied to this employer.

choices.text: Apply for PR and the work permit together, and fly when the permit comes
choices.label: BOTH

choices.text: Apply for PR only and wait in Nigeria for the decision
choices.label: WAIT
choices.feedback: AIP processing has run well over a year. Your employer needs you this winter, not in two years.

choices.text: A Toronto company DMs you. Drop the Atlantic offer
choices.label: DROPPED

AIP_WAIT.title: Still waiting.
AIP_WAIT.speaker: {area}, {city}
AIP_WAIT.dialogue: Eight months. Your employer emails: 'Any update? We'd love you here by spring.'

choices.text: Apply for the work permit after all
choices.label: LATE_PERMIT

choices.text: Keep waiting for PR
choices.label: KEPT_WAITING

AIP_LANDING.title: −8°C and a wet wind.
AIP_LANDING.speaker: Atlantic Canada, week one
AIP_LANDING.dialogue: The settlement provider that wrote your plan sends a welcome checklist: SIN, bank, health card, bus pass, newcomer orientation. Your work permit names one employer. A cousin in Toronto texts about a better-paid job, and a neighbour offers weekend cash work.

choices.text: Stay with your employer, show up early, learn how things work here
choices.label: STAYED

choices.text: Leave after month two for the Toronto job
choices.label: LEFT

choices.text: Take the weekend cash job too
choices.label: CASH_JOB

AIP_PR_WIN.title: Permanent resident, Atlantic edition.
AIP_PR_WIN.speaker: Atlantic Canada
AIP_PR_WIN.dialogue: The confirmation of permanent residence arrives. Your manager brings a cake shaped like a lobster. The settlement counsellor sends a thumbs-up.

outcome.title: Atlantic resident
outcome.subtitle: Fog, fish, and a front door that's yours.
outcome.lesson: The Atlantic Immigration Program runs on three things: a job offer from a designated employer, a settlement plan from a designated provider, and the province's endorsement. Workers never pay to be hired; the employer pays the compliance fee.

AIP_PAID_RECRUITER.title: The recruiter's number is off.
AIP_PAID_RECRUITER.speaker: {area}, {city}
AIP_PAID_RECRUITER.dialogue: Three weeks, two 'updates' and a forged offer letter later, the number is switched off.

outcome.title: Paid for a job
outcome.subtitle: CAD 3,000 gone.
outcome.lesson: AIP job offers come from designated employers, who you can find on each province's own list. Anyone selling an 'AIP job' is running a scam, and using a fake offer is misrepresentation.

AIP_FEE_SCAM.title: The 'partner agency'.
AIP_FEE_SCAM.speaker: Email
AIP_FEE_SCAM.dialogue: HR has never heard of them. The money went to a personal account.

outcome.title: The employer's fee
outcome.subtitle: You paid a fee only the employer pays.
outcome.lesson: The employer compliance fee is paid by the employer through IRCC's Employer Portal. A worker should never be asked to pay it, and requests from 'agencies' are a known scam.

AIP_FRAUD_DOCS.title: The school never sent it.
AIP_FRAUD_DOCS.speaker: WES email
AIP_FRAUD_DOCS.dialogue: WES checks with your school. Your school has no record of sending anything.

outcome.title: Printed transcript
outcome.subtitle: Misrepresentation: a five-year ban.
outcome.lesson: Transcripts must come from the school itself. A printed or altered transcript is document fraud and misrepresentation under section 40 of IRPA.

AIP_NO_OFFER.title: Not yet.
AIP_NO_OFFER.speaker: {area}, {city}
AIP_NO_OFFER.dialogue: No designated employer has endorsed you this year. Your CV is better than it was.

outcome.title: No offer yet
outcome.subtitle: Designated employers only. Keep applying.
outcome.lesson: Without a job offer from a designated employer and a strong settlement plan, there's no endorsement, and without an endorsement there's no AIP application.

AIP_LEFT.title: You jumped too soon.
AIP_LEFT.speaker: Brampton
AIP_LEFT.dialogue: The endorsement was for that job, with that employer, in that province. The PR application stalls.

outcome.title: Jumped too soon
outcome.subtitle: The endorsement was for that job.
outcome.lesson: An AIP endorsement is tied to the designated employer's job offer. Leaving it before you become a permanent resident can sink your application, and the work permit only covers that employer.

AIP_UNAUTHORIZED.title: The weekend job.
AIP_UNAUTHORIZED.speaker: A warehouse, Saturday
AIP_UNAUTHORIZED.dialogue: Cash, no paperwork. Then a workplace inspection.

outcome.title: The weekend cash job
outcome.subtitle: Your permit names one employer.
outcome.lesson: An employer-specific work permit lets you work only for the employer named on it. Unauthorized work can cost you your status and your PR application.

AIP_FUNDS_SHORT.title: Short on settlement funds.
AIP_FUNDS_SHORT.speaker: IRCC portal
AIP_FUNDS_SHORT.dialogue: You waited in Nigeria, and your savings went on rent and black tax. IRCC asks for proof of settlement funds.

outcome.title: Short on settlement funds
outcome.subtitle: The money has to be yours, and there.
outcome.lesson: AIP applicants need proof of settlement funds unless they're already living and working in Canada on a valid work permit. The amount is lower than Express Entry's, but it must be your own money.

AIP_BURNOUT.title: Burnt out.
AIP_BURNOUT.speaker: {area}, {city}
AIP_BURNOUT.dialogue: Too many portals, too little sleep, too much black tax.

outcome.title: Burnt out
outcome.subtitle: Rest, then start again.
outcome.lesson: Immigration is a long project. Pace it, budget for it, and protect your sleep.

TOURIST_WHY.title: Why are you going?
TOURIST_WHY.speaker: {area}, {city}
TOURIST_WHY.dialogue: Everybody who flies on a visitor visa has a reason. Some are going to see their children or {relName}, and coming back. Some have an invitation letter from someone in Canada who has quietly found an employer willing to talk. And some are being offered something else entirely in the group chat.

choices.text: Visit {relName} on a real visitor visa: invitation letter, return ticket, savings. See family, then come home
choices.label: FAMILY_VISIT
choices.feedback: The most common reason, and a perfectly good one. Your ties at home are why the officer said yes.

choices.text: {RelName} found an employer willing to hire. Say so on the application and go meet them in person
choices.label: MEET_EMPLOYER
choices.feedback: Visitors may meet employers and attend interviews; some do it by video instead. They can't work, and since August 2024 they generally can't get a work permit from inside Canada. The LMIA, AIP or PNP offer comes first, and the work permit application follows, usually from home.

choices.text: Tell the visa officer it's a holiday, when the real plan is to stay and find work
choices.label: PURPOSE_LIE

choices.text: A 'connect' offers an 'arranged' passport with a Canada visa inside. 'As you land, throw it away and Kawosoke'
choices.label: ARRANGED_PASSPORT

TOURIST_PURPOSE_LIE.title: The holiday that wasn't.
TOURIST_PURPOSE_LIE.speaker: CBSA secondary inspection
TOURIST_PURPOSE_LIE.dialogue: The officer reads your phone's WhatsApp, with your consent: 'Once I land, I'm not coming back.' Your visa application said a two-week holiday.

outcome.title: The holiday that wasn't
outcome.subtitle: Refused entry, and a five-year ban.
outcome.lesson: A visitor visa application must state the real purpose of the trip. Hiding a plan to stay and work is misrepresentation under section 40 of IRPA: a five-year ban. Meeting employers is allowed if you say so.

TOURIST_ARRANGED_FAIL.title: Nobody knows who you are.
TOURIST_ARRANGED_FAIL.speaker: CBSA secondary inspection
TOURIST_ARRANGED_FAIL.dialogue: You claim refugee protection with no passport and a story the 'connect' gave you. The officer's first question is who you are, and you can't prove it. You're held at the immigration holding centre while CBSA works out your identity. The person whose passport it was reported it stolen months ago.

outcome.title: The arranged passport
outcome.subtitle: Detained, no identity, and a claim nobody believes.
outcome.lesson: Travelling on an arranged or stolen passport is fraud, and throwing it away doesn't help. CBSA can detain you until your identity is established, and the Refugee Board must weigh missing documents against your credibility. People with a genuine fear can claim using their own passport and their own story.

EE_FRANCO.title: Bienvenue à Moncton.
EE_FRANCO.speaker: Video call, Moncton
EE_FRANCO.dialogue: Francophone Mobility lets an employer outside Quebec hire a French speaker without an LMIA: NCLC 5 in speaking and listening is enough. The employer submits the offer in IRCC's Employer Portal and pays the compliance fee; you apply for the work permit. A year of Canadian work then counts in Express Entry.

choices.text: Take the job, work a year in Moncton, then update your profile
choices.label: FRANCO_YEAR
choices.feedback: A year of Canadian experience, in French and English. Your CRS climbs, and the French draws want you.

choices.text: Stay in Nigeria and wait for a French draw instead
choices.label: WAIT_FRENCH

PN_RCIP.title: The community decides.
PN_RCIP.speaker: Community website, Thunder Bay
PN_RCIP.dialogue: The Rural Community Immigration Pilot replaced the old RNIP in 2025, in 14 communities. You need a job offer from an employer the community has designated, then the community's recommendation, then you apply for permanent residence directly: no Express Entry, no +600. And you must mean to live there.

choices.text: Find the community's designated employers and apply to the ones in your field
choices.label: RCIP_APPLY

choices.text: Pay an agent who sells 'community recommendations'
choices.label: PAID_RECOMMENDATION

PN_RCIP_SCAM.title: The recommendation that wasn't.
PN_RCIP_SCAM.speaker: WhatsApp
PN_RCIP_SCAM.dialogue: The 'recommendation letter' has a logo copied from the city website. The community has no record of you.

outcome.title: Bought recommendation
outcome.subtitle: Money gone; a fake document on your name.
outcome.lesson: Community recommendations come only from the community's own committee, after a job offer from a designated employer. They can't be bought, and submitting a fake one is misrepresentation.

PN_RCIP_RECOMMENDED.title: Recommended.
PN_RCIP_RECOMMENDED.speaker: Email from the community
PN_RCIP_RECOMMENDED.dialogue: A designated employer in Thunder Bay offered you the job, and the community's committee recommends you. You apply for permanent residence with the recommendation, your job offer and your language and education results.

choices.text: Apply for PR, and plan to live in Thunder Bay
choices.label: RCIP_PR

SP_START.title: Your spouse can sponsor you.
SP_START.speaker: {area}, {city}
SP_START.dialogue: Your spouse became a permanent resident in {relCity} last year, and a citizen or PR can sponsor a spouse, common-law or conjugal partner (not a fiancé). The sponsor promises to support you for three years. IRCC needs to believe one thing: the marriage is genuine and not mainly for immigration.

choices.text: Gather your real history: traditional and court wedding photos with family, years of chats, visits, money sent both ways
choices.label: REAL_HISTORY

choices.text: Your wedding was last month at the registry; traditional rites come later
choices.label: RECENT_MARRIAGE
choices.feedback: A new marriage isn't refused for being new, but expect questions. Show how the relationship grew, not just the certificate.

choices.text: A 'connect' offers a Canadian to marry you for CAD 15,000
choices.label: PAID_MARRIAGE

SP_STREAM.title: Outland or inland?
SP_STREAM.speaker: IRCC website
SP_STREAM.dialogue: Outland: you apply from Nigeria and wait here. Inland: you must already be living with your spouse in Canada, and you can get an open work permit while you wait, but a visitor visa to get there isn't guaranteed.

choices.text: Outland: apply from Nigeria, keep your job, visit when you can
choices.label: OUTLAND

choices.text: Inland: apply for a visitor visa, move in with your spouse, then apply with an open work permit
choices.label: INLAND

success.feedback: Visitor visa approved. You land and move in. The inland application goes in with an open work permit request.

fail.feedback: Visitor visa refused: the officer wasn't sure you'd leave. You apply outland instead.

SP_FORMS.title: Two people, one story.
SP_FORMS.speaker: Video call with your spouse
SP_FORMS.dialogue: The sponsor's undertaking, the relationship questionnaire, police certificates, a medical. Officers compare your answers with your spouse's: dates, places, who proposed, which church or masjid.

choices.text: Fill the questionnaire together on video, so every date matches
choices.label: TOGETHER

choices.text: Each of you fills yours alone, fast
choices.label: ALONE
choices.feedback: Your dates for the engagement differ by a year. Mismatched answers are one of the commonest reasons for an interview.

choices.text: Pay an agent to 'polish' the story with visits that never happened
choices.label: FAKE_EVIDENCE

SP_WAIT.title: The long wait.
SP_WAIT.speaker: {area}, {city}
SP_WAIT.dialogue: Spousal applications can take a year or more. Your spouse sends the rent screenshot; you send the generator one.

choices.text: Keep the relationship visible: weekly calls, a visit, both families involved
choices.label: VISIBLE

choices.text: Work full-time on your open work permit and save
choices.label: OWP_WORK

choices.text: Go quiet. The forms speak for themselves
choices.label: QUIET

SP_INTERVIEW.title: 'Tell me how you met.'
SP_INTERVIEW.speaker: Interview with an IRCC officer
SP_INTERVIEW.dialogue: The officer has both questionnaires open. 'Tell me how you met, and what your spouse did last Sunday.'

choices.text: Tell it as it happened, boring parts included
choices.label: TRUTHFUL

success.feedback: The officer smiles at the part about the borrowed phone charger. Approved.

fail.feedback: 'I'm not satisfied the relationship is genuine.' Refused, with a right to appeal.

choices.text: Recite the version you rehearsed word for word
choices.label: SCRIPTED
choices.feedback: Word-perfect and lifeless. The officer asks one follow-up question you can't answer.

SP_APPROVED.title: PPR for two.
SP_APPROVED.speaker: IRCC portal
SP_APPROVED.dialogue: Passport request. Your passport goes to the visa centre in {vacCity} and comes back with a permanent resident visa and your COPR. Your spouse is already crying on FaceTime.

choices.text: Fly to {relCity} and land together
choices.label: LAND

SP_PR.title: Together in Canada.
SP_PR.speaker: Pearson arrivals
SP_PR.dialogue: The officer stamps the COPR. Your spouse holds a sign with your name spelled wrong on purpose. Two names on one lease.

outcome.title: Together in Canada
outcome.subtitle: Sponsored, landed, home.
outcome.lesson: Spousal sponsorship works when the relationship is genuine and the file shows it: consistent answers, real history, both families. The sponsor's three-year undertaking is a legal promise of support.

SP_CONVENIENCE.title: The paid wedding.
SP_CONVENIENCE.speaker: Visa office
SP_CONVENIENCE.dialogue: The officer asks your 'spouse' your mother's name. They don't know it. They don't know your birthday either.

outcome.title: Marriage of convenience
outcome.subtitle: Refused, banned, and the sponsor is in trouble too.
outcome.lesson: A marriage entered into mainly to immigrate is a marriage of convenience: refusal, a five-year misrepresentation ban, and the sponsor can be investigated. Paid marriages are a known fraud.

SP_FAKE_STORY.title: The visits that never happened.
SP_FAKE_STORY.speaker: IRCC portal
SP_FAKE_STORY.dialogue: Your passport has no Canadian stamps for the 'visits' in the photos. The photos were edited.

outcome.title: Polished story
outcome.subtitle: Misrepresentation: a five-year ban.
outcome.lesson: Invented visits or edited photos are false evidence, even in a real marriage. Thin but true beats thick and false.

SP_REFUSED.title: Not convinced.
SP_REFUSED.speaker: IRCC portal
SP_REFUSED.dialogue: Refused. The relationship is real, but the file didn't show it.

outcome.title: Not convinced
outcome.subtitle: A real marriage, a thin file.
outcome.lesson: Officers decide on evidence. A sponsor can usually appeal a spousal refusal to the Immigration Appeal Division, or you can reapply with a stronger file.

SP_BURNOUT.title: Burnt out.
SP_BURNOUT.speaker: {area}, {city}
SP_BURNOUT.dialogue: Two time zones, one portal, no sleep.

outcome.title: Burnt out
outcome.subtitle: Rest, then pick it up together.
outcome.lesson: Long waits are normal. Pace yourselves and keep the relationship, not just the file, alive.
